skills.description: Balance equations with polyatomic ions or combustion, e.g. C3H8 + 5 O2 -> 3 CO2 + 4 H2O.

skills.name: Predict products
skills.description: Predict products using the activity series or solubility rules, e.g. Zn + CuSO4 gives ZnSO4 + Cu.

skills.name: Oxidation and reduction
skills.description: Assign oxidation numbers and identify what is oxidised and reduced, e.g. in Zn + Cu2+ zinc is oxidised.

skills.name: Moles and molar mass
skills.description: Convert between grams, moles and particles, e.g. 36 g of water is 2 mol.

skills.name: Mole ratios
skills.description: Use coefficients to find moles or grams of product, e.g. 4 mol H2 with excess O2 gives 4 mol H2O.

skills.name: Limiting reactant
skills.description: Identify the limiting reactant and the amount of product it allows, e.g. 2 mol H2 and 2 mol O2: H2 limits, 2 mol H2O.

skills.name: Percent yield and composition
skills.description: Compute percent yield or percent composition, e.g. 8 g actual of 10 g theoretical is 80%.

skills.name: Molarity and dilution
skills.description: Compute concentration or dilution volumes, e.g. 0.5 mol in 2 L is 0.25 M; M1V1 = M2V2.

skills.name: Solubility and solubility curves
skills.description: Read a solubility curve and classify a solution as unsaturated, saturated or supersaturated.

skills.name: Gas laws
skills.description: Apply Boyle's, Charles's or the combined gas law, e.g. halving the volume at constant temperature doubles the pressure.

skills.name: Ideal gas law
skills.description: Solve PV = nRT for one variable, e.g. 1 mol at 273 K and 101.3 kPa occupies about 22.4 L.

skills.name: pH and concentration
skills.description: Convert between pH and hydrogen ion concentration, e.g. 0.001 M H+ is pH 3.

skills.name: Neutralisation and titration
skills.description: Write the salt formed and compute titration concentrations, e.g. HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O; 25 mL of 0.1 M NaOH neutralises 25 mL of 0.1 M HCl.

skills.name: Factors affecting rate
skills.description: Predict how temperature, concentration, surface area or a catalyst changes rate, e.g. powdered zinc reacts faster than a lump.

skills.name: Le Chatelier's principle
skills.description: Predict the shift when concentration, pressure or temperature changes, e.g. adding reactant shifts toward products.

skills.name: Motion graphs
skills.description: Read velocity from a position-time slope or displacement from a velocity-time area, e.g. a flat velocity-time line at 4 m/s for 3 s is 12 m.

skills.name: Kinematic equations
skills.description: Solve constant-acceleration problems, e.g. from rest at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s gives 25 m.

skills.name: Projectile motion
skills.description: Compute time of flight, range or height for a projectile, e.g. dropped from 20 m it falls for about 2 s.

skills.name: Vectors and components
skills.description: Add perpendicular vectors or resolve into components, e.g. 3 m east and 4 m north give 5 m.

skills.name: Newton's laws quantitatively
skills.description: Apply F = ma and action-reaction pairs, e.g. 20 N on 5 kg gives 4 m/s^2.

skills.name: Free-body diagrams
skills.description: Choose the correct free-body diagram or the net force for a scenario, e.g. a box on a table has weight down and normal force up.

skills.name: Friction and inclines
skills.description: Compute friction or acceleration on a slope, e.g. friction = 0.2 x 50 N = 10 N.

skills.name: Circular motion and gravitation
skills.description: Compute centripetal acceleration or gravitational force, e.g. v^2/r at 10 m/s and 5 m is 20 m/s^2.

skills.name: Work and kinetic energy
skills.description: Compute work and kinetic energy, e.g. 10 N over 3 m is 30 J; 2 kg at 3 m/s has 9 J.

skills.name: Conservation of energy
skills.description: Use energy conservation to find speed or height, e.g. dropped from 5 m it hits at about 10 m/s.

skills.name: Momentum and collisions
skills.description: Apply conservation of momentum to collisions, e.g. 2 kg at 3 m/s hits 1 kg at rest and they stick at 2 m/s.

skills.name: Power and efficiency
skills.description: Compute power and efficiency, e.g. 600 J in 10 s is 60 W; 40 J useful of 100 J in is 40%.

skills.name: Wave equation and periodic motion
skills.description: Relate period, frequency, wavelength and speed, e.g. period 0.5 s is 2 Hz.

skills.name: Interference and standing waves
skills.description: Classify constructive and destructive interference and compute harmonics, e.g. a 2 m string's fundamental has wavelength 4 m.

skills.name: Reflection, refraction and Snell's law
skills.description: Apply the law of reflection and Snell's law, e.g. n1 sin i = n2 sin r.

skills.name: Lenses, mirrors and Doppler effect
skills.description: Use the thin lens equation and predict pitch shifts, e.g. an approaching siren sounds higher.

skills.name: Coulomb's law and electric fields
skills.description: Compute the force between charges or the field direction, e.g. doubling one charge doubles the force.

skills.name: Series and parallel circuits
skills.description: Compute equivalent resistance, current and voltage drops, e.g. two 6 ohm resistors in parallel give 3 ohms.

skills.name: Electrical power and energy
skills.description: Compute power and energy cost, e.g. P = IV; a 100 W bulb for 10 h uses 1 kWh.

skills.name: Capacitors
skills.description: Compute charge, capacitance or stored energy, e.g. Q = CV; 2 F at 3 V stores 6 C.

skills.name: Magnetic fields and forces
skills.description: Use the right-hand rule to find the force on a moving charge or a current-carrying wire.

skills.name: Electromagnetic induction
skills.description: Predict induced current from changing flux and compute EMF, e.g. faster coil motion gives larger EMF.

skills.name: Transformers and generators
skills.description: Compute transformer voltages from turn ratios, e.g. 100:200 turns doubles the voltage.

skills.name: Photons and the photoelectric effect
skills.description: Compute photon energy and predict electron emission, e.g. E = hf; higher frequency light ejects electrons.

skills.name: Nuclear decay and half-life
skills.description: Balance alpha and beta decay equations and compute remaining amounts, e.g. U-238 alpha decays to Th-234.

skills.name: Fission, fusion and E = mc^2
skills.description: Compare fission and fusion and compute energy from a mass defect, e.g. 1 kg of mass is 9 x 10^16 J.

skills.name: Special relativity basics
skills.description: Predict time dilation and length contraction qualitatively, e.g. a fast-moving clock runs slow to a stationary observer.

skills.name: Life cycle of stars
skills.description: Order the stages of a star's life by mass, e.g. nebula, main sequence, red giant, white dwarf for a sun-like star.

skills.name: Hertzsprung-Russell diagram
skills.description: Place a star by temperature and luminosity and classify it, e.g. hot and dim is a white dwarf.

skills.name: Evidence for the Big Bang
skills.description: Match evidence to what it shows, e.g. redshift of galaxies to expansion, cosmic microwave background to early heat.

skills.name: Kepler's laws
skills.description: Use Kepler's third law to compare periods and distances, e.g. a planet at 4 AU has a period of 8 years.

skills.name: Radiometric dating
skills.description: Compute an age from half-life and remaining fraction, e.g. 12.5% of C-14 left means about 17,190 years.

skills.name: Major events in Earth's history
skills.description: Order events such as formation of the oceans, oxygenation of the atmosphere and mass extinctions.

skills.name: Tectonics and surface processes
skills.description: Explain how plate motion, mountain building and erosion interact, e.g. uplift increases weathering which draws down CO2.

skills.name: Natural hazards and risk
skills.description: Compare hazard probability and consequence to rank risk, e.g. a 1-in-100-year flood zone with dense housing.

skills.name: Earth's energy budget
skills.description: Balance incoming and outgoing energy and compute albedo effects, e.g. 30% reflected leaves 70% absorbed.

skills.name: Greenhouse effect and feedbacks
skills.description: Classify a feedback as positive or negative, e.g. melting ice lowering albedo is a positive feedback.

skills.name: Interpret climate records
skills.description: Read ice-core, temperature or CO2 time series and compute a rate of change, e.g. 280 to 420 ppm since 1850.

skills.name: Ocean-atmosphere interactions
skills.description: Predict regional effects of El Nino, ocean acidification or circulation changes, e.g. El Nino brings rain to Peru.

skills.name: Ecological footprint and sustainability
skills.description: Compute and compare resource use per person and judge sustainability, e.g. 3 Earths needed if everyone lived like country X.

skills.name: Threats to biodiversity
skills.description: Classify a threat as habitat loss, invasive species, pollution, overharvesting or climate change, e.g. zebra mussels are invasive.

skills.name: Water and soil resources
skills.description: Evaluate water use and soil degradation data and choose a management practice, e.g. drip irrigation cuts water loss.

skills.name: Pollution and remediation
skills.description: Match a pollutant to its treatment and predict bioaccumulation, e.g. mercury concentrates in top predators.

skills.name: Compare energy sources
skills.description: Rank energy sources by carbon emissions, cost or reliability from a data table, e.g. solar has near-zero operating emissions.

skills.name: Energy efficiency calculations
skills.description: Compute efficiency and energy savings, e.g. a 35% efficient plant delivers 350 MJ from 1000 MJ of fuel.

skills.name: Carbon accounting
skills.description: Compute emissions from activity data and emission factors, e.g. 100 L of petrol is about 230 kg CO2.

skills.name: Experimental design
skills.description: Identify controls, randomisation, blinding and sample size issues in a study, e.g. a placebo group makes a drug trial controlled.

skills.name: Hypothesis testing
skills.description: Decide whether results support or refute a hypothesis and whether the claim is falsifiable, e.g. a p-value below 0.05 indicates a significant difference.

skills.name: Theories, laws and models
skills.description: Classify statements as observation, law, theory or model, e.g. plate tectonics is a theory, F = ma is a law.

skills.name: Peer review, bias and ethics
skills.description: Spot sources of bias and judge the reliability of a claim, e.g. a study funded by the product's maker needs independent replication.

skills.name: Mean, median, spread
skills.description: Compute mean, median, range or standard deviation from a small data set, e.g. mean of 4, 6, 8 is 6.

skills.name: Correlation vs causation
skills.description: Decide whether data show correlation, causation or a confounding variable, e.g. ice cream sales and drowning both rise in summer.

skills.name: Uncertainty and significant figures
skills.description: Report results with correct significant figures and percent error, e.g. measured 9.6 vs 9.8 m/s^2 is about 2% error.

skills.name: Evaluate models and predictions
skills.description: Compare a model's predictions with data and judge its fit or limits, e.g. the linear model under-predicts after year 5.

skills.name: Letter sounds
skills.description: Match a letter to the sound it makes, e.g. pick the picture that starts with the sound of 'm' (moon).

skills.name: Short vowels
skills.description: Identify the short vowel sound in a spoken CVC word, e.g. 'cat' has the short 'a' sound.

skills.name: Build and read CVC words
skills.description: Blend three letter tiles into a word that matches a picture, e.g. d-o-g for a dog.

skills.name: Rhyming words
skills.description: Pick the word that rhymes with a target word, e.g. 'hat' rhymes with 'cat' not 'cup'.

skills.name: Read high-frequency words
skills.description: Hear a high-frequency word such as 'the', 'said' or 'was' and tap it among three similar-looking words.

skills.name: Complete a sentence
skills.description: Choose the sight word that completes a simple sentence, e.g. 'I ___ a dog.' (have).

skills.name: Word categories
skills.description: Sort words into groups such as animals, food and clothes, e.g. 'apple' goes in food.

skills.name: Opposites
skills.description: Match a word to its opposite, e.g. 'hot' with 'cold'.

skills.name: Position and describing words
skills.description: Choose the word that describes a picture, e.g. the cat is 'under' the table or the ball is 'big'.

skills.name: Who, what, where
skills.description: After a two-sentence story, answer a who/what/where question, e.g. 'Where did Sam go?' (the park).

skills.name: Retell in order
skills.description: Put three story pictures or sentences in the order they happened.

skills.name: Characters and setting
skills.description: Pick the character or the setting of a short story, e.g. the story happens 'at the beach'.

skills.name: Build a sentence
skills.description: Arrange word tiles into a complete sentence, e.g. 'The dog runs fast.'

skills.name: Capital letter and end mark
skills.description: Choose the correctly written sentence that starts with a capital and ends with a period or question mark.

skills.name: Naming words and action words
skills.description: Sort words into nouns (things) and verbs (actions), e.g. 'jump' is an action word.

skills.name: Singular and plural
skills.description: Choose the plural for a picture of more than one thing, e.g. one cat, two 'cats'.

skills.name: Simple pronouns
skills.description: Replace a name with the right pronoun, e.g. 'Anna is happy' becomes 'She is happy'.

skills.name: Short and long vowels
skills.description: Decide whether a word has a short or long vowel sound and spell the silent-e pattern, e.g. 'cap' vs 'cape'.

skills.name: Blends and digraphs
skills.description: Complete a word with the right blend or digraph, e.g. '__ip' with 'sh' for a picture of a ship.

skills.name: Vowel teams
skills.description: Choose the vowel team that spells a word, e.g. 'r_n' with 'ai' for rain, not 'ae'.

skills.name: R-controlled vowels
skills.description: Sort words by their r-controlled sound (ar, or, er/ir/ur), e.g. 'bird' and 'fern' share a sound.

skills.name: Spell sight words
skills.description: Hear a high-frequency word such as 'because' or 'friend' and spell it with letter tiles.

skills.name: Irregular plurals
skills.description: Give the plural of an irregular noun, e.g. 'child' becomes 'children'.

skills.name: Endings -ed, -ing, -s
skills.description: Add the ending correctly, doubling or dropping letters when needed, e.g. 'hop' + ing = 'hopping'.

skills.name: Compound words
skills.description: Join two small words to make a compound word that matches a clue, e.g. 'sun' + 'flower'.

skills.name: Synonyms and antonyms
skills.description: Pick a word that means the same as or the opposite of a target, e.g. 'tiny' is a synonym of 'small'.

skills.name: Context clues
skills.description: Use the rest of a sentence to pick the meaning of an unknown word, e.g. 'The gigantic dog was bigger than the car' means very big.

skills.name: Beginning, middle, end
skills.description: Order the events of a short story or label which part is the beginning, middle or end.

skills.name: How characters respond
skills.description: Explain how a character feels or acts after an event, e.g. Mia felt 'proud' after finishing the race.

skills.name: Lesson of a fable
skills.description: Choose the lesson a fable or folktale teaches, e.g. 'Slow and steady wins the race'.

skills.name: Main topic
skills.description: Pick the main topic of a short paragraph, e.g. a paragraph about how bees make honey.

skills.name: Text features
skills.description: Identify what a caption, heading, glossary or bold word is for, e.g. use the glossary to find a word's meaning.

skills.name: Find a detail
skills.description: Locate the detail in a passage that answers a question, e.g. 'How many legs does a spider have?'

skills.name: Opinion with a reason
skills.description: Match an opinion to a reason that supports it, e.g. 'Dogs are the best pets because they are loyal'.

skills.name: Order words in narratives
skills.description: Choose the right order word (first, next, then, finally) to join the steps of a story.

skills.name: Expand a sentence
skills.description: Add a describing word or detail to make a sentence more interesting, e.g. 'The dog ran' to 'The brown dog ran quickly'.

skills.name: Adjectives and adverbs
skills.description: Choose whether an adjective or adverb fits, e.g. 'She sings ___' needs 'beautifully'.

skills.name: Past tense verbs
skills.description: Give the past tense of regular and common irregular verbs, e.g. 'run' becomes 'ran'.

skills.name: Contractions and possessives
skills.description: Form a contraction or possessive with an apostrophe, e.g. 'do not' is 'don't' and the dog's bone.

skills.name: Capitalize names and dates
skills.description: Pick the sentence with correct capitals for names, holidays and places, e.g. 'We visited Paris in July'.

skills.name: Read multisyllable words
skills.description: Hear a longer word such as 'remember' and pick its correct written form among near-misspellings.

skills.name: Irregularly spelled words
skills.description: Read and spell irregular words like 'enough', 'though' and 'island'.

skills.name: Syllables
skills.description: Split a word into syllables or count them, e.g. 'bas-ket-ball' has three syllables.

skills.name: Homophones
skills.description: Choose the correct homophone for a sentence, e.g. 'their', 'there' or 'they're'.

skills.name: Suffix spelling rules
skills.description: Add a suffix with the right change, e.g. 'happy' + ness = 'happiness' (y to i).

skills.name: Prefixes and suffixes
skills.description: Build or decode a word from a prefix or suffix and a base, e.g. 'un' + 'happy' means not happy.

skills.name: Context clues
skills.description: Use sentence clues to choose the meaning of an unfamiliar word in a short passage.

skills.name: Shades of meaning
skills.description: Order related words by intensity, e.g. 'warm', 'hot', 'scorching'.

skills.name: Literal and nonliteral
skills.description: Decide what a nonliteral phrase means, e.g. 'It's raining cats and dogs' means raining hard.

skills.name: Central message
skills.description: Pick the central message or lesson of a short fable, myth or story and the detail that shows it.

skills.name: Character traits and motivation
skills.description: Choose a trait or motive for a character from their actions, e.g. sharing lunch shows 'generous'.

skills.name: Narrator's point of view
skills.description: Tell whether a passage is told by a character ('I') or a narrator, and how it differs from your own view.

skills.name: Main idea and details
skills.description: Choose the main idea of a paragraph and sort sentences into main idea versus supporting detail.

skills.name: Cause and effect
skills.description: Match a cause to its effect in a passage, e.g. 'It rained' leads to 'the game was cancelled'.

skills.name: Steps in a process
skills.description: Order the steps of a how-to text, e.g. the stages of a butterfly's life cycle.

skills.name: Topic sentence and details
skills.description: Pick the topic sentence for a paragraph or arrange sentences so the topic sentence comes first.

skills.name: Linking words
skills.description: Choose a linking word that connects ideas, e.g. 'also', 'because', 'but', 'therefore'.

skills.name: Dialogue in narratives
skills.description: Pick the correctly punctuated line of dialogue, e.g. "Let's go," said Max.

skills.name: Verb tenses
skills.description: Choose the past, present or future form of a verb to fit a sentence, e.g. 'Tomorrow I will walk'.

skills.name: Subject-verb agreement
skills.description: Pick the verb that agrees with the subject, e.g. 'The dogs ___' takes 'bark' not 'barks'.

skills.name: Comparative and superlative
skills.description: Form comparisons correctly, e.g. 'big', 'bigger', 'biggest' and 'more careful'.

skills.name: Commas and quotation marks
skills.description: Place commas in addresses and dates and quotation marks around speech, e.g. 'Austin, Texas'.

skills.name: Make inferences
skills.description: Use clues in a passage to infer something not stated, e.g. wet umbrellas by the door mean it rained.

skills.name: Summarize
skills.description: Choose the best one-sentence summary of a passage, avoiding minor details.

skills.name: Determine theme
skills.description: Identify the theme of a story or poem from details, e.g. perseverance pays off.

skills.name: Identify structure
skills.description: Classify a paragraph as chronology, comparison, cause/effect or problem/solution.

skills.name: Signal words
skills.description: Match signal words to structures, e.g. 'however' signals comparison and 'as a result' signals effect.

skills.name: Firsthand and secondhand accounts
skills.description: Decide whether an account is firsthand (eyewitness) or secondhand (reporter) from its wording.

skills.name: Poetry, drama and prose
skills.description: Identify structural elements such as verse, stanza, cast of characters and stage directions.

skills.name: Describe characters and settings
skills.description: Pick the specific detail (thought, word or action) that supports a description of a character.

skills.name: Compare stories
skills.description: Compare the themes or patterns of events in two short stories, e.g. two quests for a lost object.

skills.name: Greek and Latin roots
skills.description: Use a root to find meaning, e.g. 'tele' (far) + 'graph' (write) suggests writing from afar.

skills.name: Context clues
skills.description: Choose the meaning of a word from definition, example or restatement clues in a passage.

skills.name: Idioms, adages and proverbs
skills.description: Pick the meaning of a common idiom or proverb, e.g. 'the early bird catches the worm'.

skills.name: Similes and metaphors
skills.description: Tell a simile from a metaphor and explain what is compared, e.g. 'as busy as a bee'.

skills.name: Relative pronouns and adverbs
skills.description: Choose who, whose, which, that, where or when to complete a sentence.

skills.name: Progressive tenses
skills.description: Form 'was walking', 'is walking' or 'will be walking' to fit the time of a sentence.

skills.name: Modal auxiliaries
skills.description: Pick can, may, must or should to convey ability, permission or obligation.

skills.name: Fragments and run-ons
skills.description: Classify a sentence as complete, fragment or run-on and choose the fix.

skills.name: Commas and quotations
skills.description: Punctuate direct speech and compound sentences, e.g. 'I ran, but I missed the bus.'

skills.name: Frequently confused words
skills.description: Choose between to/too/two, your/you're, its/it's in context.

skills.name: Order of adjectives
skills.description: Arrange adjectives in conventional order, e.g. 'a small red bag' not 'a red small bag'.

skills.name: Opinion with grouped reasons
skills.description: Sort reasons and facts under the opinion they support and pick the strongest reason.

skills.name: Organize an informative text
skills.description: Group related facts under headings and order paragraphs logically.

skills.name: Narrative details
skills.description: Choose sensory details and dialogue that develop a scene, e.g. 'the crunch of frosty grass'.

skills.name: Choose a source
skills.description: Pick which source (encyclopedia, atlas, interview, website) best answers a research question.

skills.name: Take and sort notes
skills.description: Sort note cards into the categories of a research topic, e.g. habitat, diet, predators.

skills.name: Quote evidence
skills.description: Select the quotation from a passage that best supports an inference or answer.

skills.name: Compare themes and topics
skills.description: Compare how two stories in the same genre treat a theme, e.g. two tales about courage.

skills.name: Narrator's influence
skills.description: Describe how the narrator's point of view shapes the events described, e.g. a biased first-person narrator.

skills.name: Compare structures
skills.description: Compare the structure of two texts on the same topic, e.g. chronological versus problem/solution.

skills.name: Multiple accounts
skills.description: Note similarities and differences in how two accounts of the same event present the facts.

skills.name: Relationships between ideas
skills.description: Explain how two people, events or ideas in a text are related using specific details.

skills.name: Interpret metaphors and similes
skills.description: Explain what a metaphor or simile means in context, e.g. 'the classroom was a zoo' means noisy and chaotic.

skills.name: Idioms and proverbs
skills.description: Match idioms and proverbs to their meanings and use them in sentences.

skills.name: Personification and hyperbole
skills.description: Identify personification or hyperbole and what it suggests, e.g. 'the wind whispered'.

skills.name: Roots and affixes
skills.description: Decode words with Greek and Latin parts, e.g. 'photosynthesis' from 'photo' (light) and 'syn' (together).

skills.name: Multiple-meaning words
skills.description: Choose the meaning of a word with several senses from context, e.g. 'bark' of a tree or a dog.

skills.name: Advanced context clues
skills.description: Use comparison, contrast and cause/effect clues in a sentence to determine a word's meaning.

skills.name: Conjunctions, prepositions, interjections
skills.description: Identify or supply the correct conjunction, preposition or interjection in a sentence.

skills.name: Perfect tenses
skills.description: Form 'had walked', 'has walked' or 'will have walked' to fit a sentence.

skills.name: Inappropriate tense shifts
skills.description: Spot and correct a sentence that shifts tense, e.g. 'She ran home and eats dinner'.

skills.name: Correlative conjunctions
skills.description: Use pairs such as either/or and neither/nor correctly in a sentence.

skills.name: Commas in series and introductions
skills.description: Place commas in a list and after introductory words, e.g. 'Yes, I like apples, pears, and plums.'

skills.name: Titles of works
skills.description: Choose underlining/italics or quotation marks for a title, e.g. a book versus a poem.

skills.name: Commas for direct address and tag questions
skills.description: Punctuate 'Thank you, Sam' and 'It's cold, isn't it?' correctly.

skills.name: Opinion essay structure
skills.description: Order the parts of an opinion essay: introduction with claim, reasons with evidence, conclusion.

skills.name: Facts, definitions and quotations
skills.description: Choose the fact, definition or quotation that develops an informative paragraph's point.

skills.name: Narrative pacing and transitions
skills.description: Choose transitions and sentence lengths that manage pace, e.g. short sentences for action.

skills.name: Paraphrase versus copy
skills.description: Pick the paraphrase that restates a source accurately in new words without copying.

skills.name: List sources
skills.description: Match a source type to the information needed to cite it, e.g. a website needs the URL and date accessed.

skills.name: Relevant information
skills.description: Decide whether a fact is relevant to a research question, e.g. a shark's diet for a report on its habitat.

skills.name: Cite evidence for inferences
skills.description: Choose the textual evidence that best supports an inference about a character or idea.

skills.name: Theme and objective summary
skills.description: Pick the theme and the summary free of personal opinion for a passage.

skills.name: Plot and character development
skills.description: Order plot events and explain how a character changes as the plot moves toward resolution.

skills.name: Role of a sentence or chapter
skills.description: Explain how a sentence, stanza or chapter fits into the whole, e.g. it introduces the conflict.

skills.name: Author's point of view and purpose
skills.description: Determine an author's purpose or viewpoint and how it is conveyed, e.g. to persuade readers to recycle.

skills.name: Trace an argument
skills.description: Separate claims supported by evidence from unsupported ones in a short argument.

skills.name: Connotation and denotation
skills.description: Choose the word with the intended connotation, e.g. 'thrifty' versus 'stingy'.

skills.name: Figurative meaning in context
skills.description: Interpret a metaphor, personification or hyperbole as used in a passage.

skills.name: Word choice and tone
skills.description: Identify the tone created by an author's word choice, e.g. 'gloomy' and 'dreary' make a somber tone.

skills.name: Greek and Latin roots
skills.description: Use roots such as 'aud', 'bene', 'chron' to decode unfamiliar academic words.

skills.name: Affixes and parts of speech
skills.description: Predict how an affix changes meaning or part of speech, e.g. '-ify' turns 'solid' into a verb.

skills.name: Reference materials
skills.description: Read a dictionary entry to pick pronunciation, part of speech or the sense that fits a sentence.

skills.name: Parts of speech
skills.description: Tap the word in a sentence that is the noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition or conjunction asked for.

skills.name: Subject-verb agreement
skills.description: Choose the verb that agrees with a tricky subject, e.g. 'Each of the players ___' takes 'is'.

skills.name: Pronoun-antecedent agreement
skills.description: Fix a pronoun that does not match its antecedent in number or has a vague reference.

skills.name: Pronoun case
skills.description: Choose subjective, objective or possessive case, e.g. 'between you and me' not 'you and I'.

skills.name: Commas, parentheses and dashes
skills.description: Set off a nonrestrictive element with commas, parentheses or dashes, e.g. 'My cat, a tabby, sleeps all day.'

skills.name: Spell academic words
skills.description: Spell commonly misspelled words correctly, e.g. 'necessary', 'separate', 'definitely'.

skills.name: Claim and relevant evidence
skills.description: Match a claim to the evidence that supports it and discard irrelevant evidence.

skills.name: Develop with facts and examples
skills.description: Choose the fact, definition, detail or quotation that best develops a topic sentence.

skills.name: Narrative techniques
skills.description: Identify dialogue, pacing and description in a passage and pick a transition that signals a time shift.

skills.name: Assess credibility
skills.description: Rate a source's credibility from its author, date and publisher, e.g. a museum site versus an anonymous blog.

skills.name: Basic citation
skills.description: Order the parts of a simple bibliographic citation: author, title, publisher, year.

skills.name: Several pieces of evidence
skills.description: Select two or more pieces of evidence that together support an analysis of a passage.

skills.name: Theme development
skills.description: Trace how a theme develops across a passage by ordering key moments.

skills.name: Interaction of story elements
skills.description: Explain how setting shapes characters or plot, e.g. a storm forcing a decision.

skills.name: Poetic form
skills.description: Identify a sonnet, haiku or free verse and how rhyme scheme or meter contributes to meaning.

skills.name: Drama structure
skills.description: Explain how a scene, soliloquy or stage direction contributes to meaning in a play excerpt.

skills.name: Contrasting points of view
skills.description: Describe how an author develops and contrasts the viewpoints of two characters or narrators.

skills.name: Trace and evaluate an argument
skills.description: Identify the claim, reasons and evidence in a short argument and judge whether the reasoning is sound.

skills.name: Sufficient and relevant evidence
skills.description: Decide whether given evidence is relevant and sufficient for a claim, e.g. one anecdote is not enough.

skills.name: Authors' differing emphasis
skills.description: Compare how two authors writing about the same topic emphasize different evidence or facts.

skills.name: Roots and context
skills.description: Combine a Latin or Greek root with context clues to define a word, e.g. 'benevolent' in a sentence about kindness.

skills.name: Allusions
skills.description: Recognize a literary, biblical or mythological allusion and its meaning, e.g. 'an Achilles heel'.

skills.name: Analogies
skills.description: Complete a word analogy, e.g. 'glove is to hand as sock is to ___'.

skills.name: Precise and concise language
skills.description: Replace wordy or vague phrasing with a precise word, e.g. 'walked slowly and tiredly' becomes 'trudged'.

skills.name: Clauses and sentence types
skills.description: Classify a sentence as simple, compound, complex or compound-complex and identify its independent and dependent clauses.

skills.name: Phrases
skills.description: Identify prepositional, appositive and participial phrases and their function in a sentence.

skills.name: Misplaced and dangling modifiers
skills.description: Spot a misplaced modifier and choose the corrected sentence, e.g. 'Running late, the bus was missed'.

skills.name: Commas and semicolons
skills.description: Choose where a comma, a semicolon or no punctuation belongs when joining clauses, e.g. 'It rained; we stayed in.'

skills.name: Commas with coordinate adjectives
skills.description: Decide whether two adjectives need a comma, e.g. 'a small, old house' but 'a bright red car'.

skills.name: Colons and quoted material
skills.description: Introduce a list or quotation with a colon and punctuate quotations inside sentences correctly.

skills.name: Acknowledge counterclaims
skills.description: Pick the sentence that fairly acknowledges an opposing claim before rebutting it.

skills.name: Transitions and cohesion
skills.description: Choose transitions that clarify relationships between ideas, e.g. 'in contrast', 'consequently'.

skills.name: Establish point of view
skills.description: Identify first-, second- or third-person narration and keep it consistent across a passage.

skills.name: Effective search terms
skills.description: Choose the search query most likely to find relevant, specific results for a research question.

skills.name: Paraphrase and avoid plagiarism
skills.description: Decide whether a passage is properly paraphrased, quoted or plagiarized.

skills.name: Focused research question
skills.description: Pick the research question that is neither too broad nor too narrow, e.g. about one cause of coral bleaching.

skills.name: Strongest evidence
skills.description: Choose the single strongest piece of evidence for an analysis among several relevant ones.

skills.name: Dialogue and incidents
skills.description: Explain how a line of dialogue or an incident reveals character or provokes a decision.

skills.name: Dramatic irony and suspense
skills.description: Identify how a difference between audience and character knowledge creates suspense or humor.

skills.name: Role of a paragraph
skills.description: Analyze how a specific sentence or paragraph develops and refines a key concept.

skills.name: Compare two texts' structures
skills.description: Compare the structure of two texts and how each contributes to meaning and style.

skills.name: Choice of medium
skills.description: Evaluate the advantages of print, video or audio for presenting a topic, e.g. a chart for data trends.

skills.name: Sound reasoning
skills.description: Judge whether the reasoning in a claim is sound and the evidence sufficient, flagging weak links.

skills.name: Irrelevant evidence
skills.description: Identify evidence that is irrelevant to a claim even if it sounds impressive.

skills.name: Conflicting information
skills.description: Determine where two texts disagree on facts or interpretation and which is better supported.

skills.name: Roots in academic vocabulary
skills.description: Use roots and affixes to define academic words such as 'contradict', 'circumvent', 'synthesis'.

skills.name: Verbal irony and puns
skills.description: Recognize verbal irony or a pun and explain the double meaning, e.g. 'Lovely weather' during a storm.

skills.name: Nuances in meaning
skills.description: Distinguish among near-synonyms by connotation, e.g. 'bullheaded', 'willful', 'firm', 'persistent'.

skills.name: Active and passive voice
skills.description: Identify whether a sentence is active or passive and convert between them, e.g. 'The ball was kicked by Lee' to 'Lee kicked the ball'.

skills.name: Gerunds, participles and infinitives
skills.description: Identify the function of a verbal in a sentence, e.g. 'Swimming is fun' uses a gerund as subject.

skills.name: Verb moods
skills.description: Classify a sentence as indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional or subjunctive.

skills.name: Shifts in voice and mood
skills.description: Correct inappropriate shifts in voice or mood within a sentence.

skills.name: Comma, ellipsis and dash for a pause
skills.description: Choose the comma, ellipsis or dash that indicates a pause or break, e.g. a dash for an abrupt interruption.

skills.name: Ellipsis for omission
skills.description: Use an ellipsis correctly to shorten a quotation without changing its meaning.

skills.name: Organize an argument
skills.description: Order claim, evidence, counterclaim, rebuttal and conclusion into a logical argument.

skills.name: Formatting and graphics
skills.description: Choose headings, graphics or multimedia that aid comprehension of an informative text.

skills.name: Reflection and resolution
skills.description: Pick the conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated events.

skills.name: Formal style
skills.description: Replace informal wording with formal, objective phrasing, e.g. 'kids' becomes 'students'.

skills.name: Evaluate sources
skills.description: Judge accuracy and credibility of print and digital sources using author, evidence, date and bias.

skills.name: Citation format
skills.description: Pick the correctly formatted citation for a book, article or website in a standard style.

skills.name: Integrate quotations
skills.description: Choose the sentence that smoothly introduces and cites a quotation.

skills.name: Strong and thorough evidence
skills.description: Select explicit and inferential evidence that supports an analysis of a literary or informational passage.

skills.name: Central idea development
skills.description: Trace how a central idea emerges and is refined by specific details across a passage.

skills.name: Complex characters
skills.description: Analyze how a character with conflicting motivations develops and advances the plot or theme.

skills.name: Theme development
skills.description: Determine a theme and analyze how specific details shape and refine it over the course of a text.

skills.name: Structure, pacing and flashback
skills.description: Analyze how an author's choices about order, pacing or flashback create tension or surprise.

skills.name: Transformation of source material
skills.description: Analyze how a work draws on and transforms a myth, play or earlier story, e.g. a modern retelling of Romeo and Juliet.

skills.name: Ethos, pathos, logos
skills.description: Name the appeal a statement relies on, e.g. 'As a doctor with 20 years of experience...' is ethos.

skills.name: Audience and purpose
skills.description: Identify the intended audience and purpose of a speech or ad and how word choice targets them.

skills.name: Structure of an argument
skills.description: Analyze how an author orders ideas and sentences to make points clear and convincing.

skills.name: Claim, evidence, reasoning
skills.description: Build or order a full CER chain, e.g. claim, then supporting evidence, then reasoning that links the two.

skills.name: Counterclaims
skills.description: Distinguish a claim from a counterclaim and pick the rebuttal that addresses it directly.

skills.name: Evaluate evidence
skills.description: Judge whether evidence is valid, relevant and sufficient, spotting false statements and gaps.

skills.name: Academic words in context
skills.description: Determine the meaning of grade-level academic words from context, e.g. 'ambiguous', 'implicit'.

skills.name: Patterns of word changes
skills.description: Identify related forms and parts of speech, e.g. 'analyze', 'analysis', 'analytical'.

skills.name: Connotative meanings
skills.description: Analyze the cumulative impact of connotative word choices on meaning and tone.

skills.name: Parallel structure
skills.description: Fix faulty parallelism, e.g. 'She likes hiking, swimming, and to bike' to 'and biking'.

skills.name: Phrases and clauses for variety
skills.description: Combine sentences using participial, absolute or adverbial elements to vary style.

skills.name: Semicolons and colons
skills.description: Use a semicolon with a conjunctive adverb or a colon before a list or explanation correctly.

skills.name: Argument essay
skills.description: Order the sections of an argument essay with precise claims, fair counterclaims and a cohesive conclusion.

skills.name: Literary analysis paragraph
skills.description: Choose the quotation and commentary that support an analytical thesis about a text.

skills.name: Thesis statements
skills.description: Pick the thesis that is arguable, specific and previews the essay's structure.

skills.name: Primary and secondary sources
skills.description: Classify sources as primary or secondary and pick the type a question requires, e.g. a diary for a soldier's view.

skills.name: MLA citation basics
skills.description: Build a correct MLA works-cited entry and in-text citation from its parts.

skills.name: Integrate research evidence
skills.description: Choose the sentence that integrates a source smoothly while maintaining the flow of ideas.

skills.name: Inference where text is uncertain
skills.description: Decide which inferences are well supported when a passage leaves matters uncertain.

skills.name: Objective summary
skills.description: Pick the summary that captures central ideas without opinion or minor detail.

skills.name: Cultural point of view
skills.description: Analyze a point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of world literature.

skills.name: Figurative and connotative meaning
skills.description: Analyze how figurative and connotative language shapes meaning and tone in a passage.

skills.name: Author's structural choices
skills.description: Explain how choices about structure, such as parallel plots or in medias res, create effects.

skills.name: Representation across media
skills.description: Compare how a subject or scene is treated in two media, e.g. a poem and a painting.

skills.name: Rhetorical devices
skills.description: Name the device used in a sentence, e.g. anaphora, antithesis, rhetorical question, parallelism.

skills.name: Persuasive techniques
skills.description: Identify bandwagon, testimonial, loaded language or fear appeals in advertising and speeches.

skills.name: Analyze a speech
skills.description: Analyze how a speaker's rhetoric advances purpose and point of view in a famous speech excerpt.

skills.name: Logical fallacies
skills.description: Name the fallacy in a statement, e.g. straw man, ad hominem, slippery slope, false dilemma.

skills.name: Evaluate reasoning
skills.description: Decide whether a conclusion follows from its premises and identify the weak premise.

skills.name: Rebuttal and concession
skills.description: Choose the rebuttal that concedes a valid point and still defends the claim.

skills.name: Academic vocabulary
skills.description: Define academic and domain words such as 'juxtapose', 'paradigm', 'empirical' in context.

skills.name: Etymology
skills.description: Trace a word's origin to its meaning, e.g. 'philanthropy' from Greek 'love of humankind'.

skills.name: Nuance among synonyms
skills.description: Choose the synonym whose nuance fits the register and meaning of a sentence.

skills.name: Advanced punctuation
skills.description: Use semicolons, colons, dashes and hyphens in compound modifiers correctly, e.g. 'well-known author'.

skills.name: Sentence combining for style
skills.description: Combine choppy sentences into a fluent one without changing meaning.

skills.name: Follow a style manual
skills.description: Apply a style guide rule for numbers, titles or abbreviations, e.g. spell out numbers under ten.

skills.name: Synthesize two sources
skills.description: Choose the sentence that connects evidence from two sources to one point.

skills.name: Explain a complex topic
skills.description: Order explanations, examples and definitions to build understanding of a complex concept.

skills.name: Revise for clarity
skills.description: Pick the revision that fixes a vague, wordy or ambiguous sentence.

skills.name: Detect bias
skills.description: Identify loaded language, omission or one-sided sourcing that reveals bias in a text or headline.

skills.name: Evaluate online sources
skills.description: Apply authority, accuracy, currency and purpose checks to rank sources for a research task.

skills.name: Fact, opinion and claim
skills.description: Classify statements as verifiable fact, opinion or unsupported claim.

skills.name: Literary devices
skills.description: Identify the device at work in a line, e.g. irony, foreshadowing, symbolism, motif, juxtaposition, and its effect.

skills.name: Interacting themes
skills.description: Analyze how two or more themes interact and build on one another in a text.

skills.name: Satire, sarcasm and understatement
skills.description: Distinguish what is directly stated from what is really meant in satire or understatement.

skills.name: Literary periods
skills.description: Match a passage to its literary period or movement by its features, e.g. Romanticism, Modernism.

skills.name: Tone and diction
skills.description: Identify the tone of a passage and the specific diction that creates it, e.g. 'reverent' from 'hallowed' and 'solemn'.

skills.name: Syntax and effect
skills.description: Analyze how sentence length, inversion or fragments create emphasis or pace.

skills.name: Rhetoric of foundational documents
skills.description: Analyze the premises, purposes and rhetorical features of a historical speech or founding document.

skills.name: Premises and assumptions
skills.description: Identify the unstated assumption an argument depends on, e.g. that cost is the only concern.

skills.name: Evaluate legal and public reasoning
skills.description: Assess the reasoning in a court opinion or public argument for consistency and use of evidence.

skills.name: Qualify claims
skills.description: Choose the hedge or qualifier that makes an overstated claim defensible, e.g. 'most' instead of 'all'.

skills.name: Ambiguity and multiple readings
skills.description: Decide which of two interpretations a passage supports, or whether it deliberately supports both.

skills.name: Structure and aesthetic impact
skills.description: Analyze how a choice about where to begin or end a story contributes to its meaning and impact.

skills.name: Sound and image in poetry
skills.description: Identify meter, alliteration, assonance, enjambment or imagery and their effect in a poem.

skills.name: Integrate multiple sources
skills.description: Sort evidence from several sources by the position it supports and pick the strongest for each.

skills.name: Compare perspectives
skills.description: Identify where two texts agree, disagree or address different aspects of an issue.

skills.name: Thesis from sources
skills.description: Choose the thesis that accounts for the evidence in all provided sources rather than one.

skills.name: Precise diction
skills.description: Select the word whose exact meaning and register fit an academic or literary sentence.

skills.name: Etymology and shifting meaning
skills.description: Explain how a word's meaning has shifted over time, e.g. 'awful' once meant awe-inspiring.

skills.name: Domain-specific terms
skills.description: Define literary and rhetorical terms such as 'motif', 'syntax', 'allegory' and apply them to examples.

skills.name: Voice and register
skills.description: Rewrite or choose a sentence to match a target register, e.g. formal academic versus conversational.

skills.name: Concision
skills.description: Cut redundancy and filler, e.g. 'due to the fact that' becomes 'because'.

skills.name: Hyphenation and conventions
skills.description: Apply hyphenation and other conventions correctly, e.g. 'twenty-one' and 'self-aware'.

skills.name: MLA and APA citations
skills.description: Build correct MLA and APA references and in-text citations and tell the two styles apart.

skills.name: Source reliability
skills.description: Weigh a source's strengths and limitations for a specific task, audience and purpose.

skills.name: Visual and media rhetoric
skills.description: Analyze how images, layout and framing in media persuade, e.g. a cropped photo shifting the story.

skills.name: Critical lenses
skills.description: Apply a critical lens (feminist, historical, psychological, Marxist) to interpret a passage and name the lens used.

skills.name: Archetypes and allusions
skills.description: Identify archetypes and allusions such as the hero's journey or a Promethean figure and their function.

skills.name: Poetic form and meter
skills.description: Identify form and meter, e.g. iambic pentameter, villanelle, blank verse, and how form shapes meaning.

skills.name: Texts across eras
skills.description: Compare how two works from different eras treat a similar theme or topic.

skills.name: Rhetorical strategies
skills.description: Analyze how a writer's combined choices of appeal, device and structure achieve a purpose.

skills.name: Kairos and context
skills.description: Explain how timing and historical context make a rhetorical choice effective.

skills.name: Rhetorical analysis essay
skills.description: Order the parts of a rhetorical analysis: context, thesis on strategies, evidence with commentary, conclusion.

skills.name: Logical validity
skills.description: Determine whether a syllogism is valid and sound, e.g. all A are B, C is A, therefore C is B.

skills.name: Construct an argument
skills.description: Assemble claim, evidence, warrant, counterclaim and rebuttal into a coherent argument.

skills.name: Evaluate competing arguments
skills.description: Decide which of two arguments is better supported and explain the decisive factor.

skills.name: Dense and archaic prose
skills.description: Paraphrase a complex or archaic sentence accurately, e.g. a line from an 18th-century essay.

skills.name: Multiple interpretations
skills.description: Evaluate two interpretations of a text and identify the evidence that supports each.

skills.name: Implicit meaning
skills.description: Infer what a text implies through tone, irony or omission rather than direct statement.

skills.name: Weigh sources
skills.description: Rank sources by relevance and credibility for a given claim and justify the order.

skills.name: Synthesis essay
skills.description: Choose how to position several sources in relation to a thesis: support, complicate or counter.

skills.name: Resolve conflicting sources
skills.description: Explain why two credible sources disagree and how a writer should handle the disagreement.

skills.name: Diction for audience
skills.description: Choose the diction that fits a specified audience and purpose, e.g. a grant proposal versus a blog.

skills.name: Sentence variety and rhythm
skills.description: Revise a paragraph to vary sentence openings and lengths for rhythm and emphasis.

skills.name: Edit for conventions
skills.description: Find and fix the error in usage, agreement or punctuation in a college-level sentence.

skills.name: Misinformation and manipulation
skills.description: Identify misleading techniques such as cherry-picking, false context or manipulated images.

skills.name: Read data and visuals critically
skills.description: Spot a misleading chart, e.g. a truncated axis exaggerating a difference.

skills.name: Audience, platform and algorithms
skills.description: Explain how platform and algorithmic curation shape which messages an audience sees.

skills.name: Refine a research question
skills.description: Narrow a broad topic into a researchable question and pick the most focused version.

skills.name: Annotated bibliography
skills.description: Match a source's citation to an annotation that summarizes and evaluates it.

skills.name: Citation and academic integrity
skills.description: Decide whether a use of a source needs a citation and choose the correct format for it.

skills.name: Family roles
skills.description: Identify who does what in a family, e.g. pick which family member in a picture is a grandparent or match 'cooks dinner' to a role.

skills.name: Family traditions
skills.description: Recognise traditions families share such as meals, songs or celebrations, e.g. choose which picture shows a birthday tradition.

skills.name: Families then and now
skills.description: Sort everyday objects and activities into 'long ago' or 'today', e.g. a candle lamp vs an electric lamp.

skills.name: Community helpers
skills.description: Match community helpers to their jobs and tools, e.g. firefighter to fire truck, doctor to stethoscope.

skills.name: Places in a community
skills.description: Identify what happens at common places such as a school, library, hospital or post office, e.g. 'Where do you borrow books?'.

skills.name: Why we have rules
skills.description: Choose the rule that keeps people safe or fair in a given situation, e.g. 'What rule helps everyone hear the teacher?'.

skills.name: Fair and unfair
skills.description: Decide whether a short scenario is fair or unfair and pick a fair solution, e.g. two children want the same toy.

skills.name: Leaders around us
skills.description: Identify leaders in school and community and what they do, e.g. match 'principal' to 'leads the school'.

skills.name: Map symbols
skills.description: Read simple picture symbols on a classroom or neighbourhood map, e.g. tap the symbol that means 'park'.

skills.name: Position words
skills.description: Use near, far, left, right, above and below to locate objects on a simple map, e.g. 'What is next to the school?'.

skills.name: Land and water on a globe
skills.description: Tell land from water on a globe or map and know a globe is a model of Earth, e.g. 'Is the blue part land or water?'.

skills.name: Needs vs wants
skills.description: Sort items into needs and wants, e.g. water and a coat are needs, a video game is a want.

skills.name: Goods and services
skills.description: Sort examples into goods (things) and services (work done for others), e.g. an apple vs a haircut.

skills.name: Jobs and money
skills.description: Understand that people work to earn money to buy things, e.g. choose what a baker sells to earn money.

skills.name: Days, months, seasons
skills.description: Order days of the week and months of the year and link seasons to months, e.g. put Monday to Friday in order.

skills.name: Before and after
skills.description: Put three or four daily or life events in time order, e.g. baby, child, grown-up.

skills.name: National symbols
skills.description: Recognise a country's flag, anthem and famous landmarks, e.g. pick the flag that belongs to your country.

skills.name: Holidays and their meaning
skills.description: Match common national and world holidays to what they celebrate, e.g. Independence Day to a country's birthday.

skills.name: Urban, suburban, rural
skills.description: Sort pictures and descriptions into city, suburb and countryside, e.g. tall buildings and buses are urban.

skills.name: Neighbourhood maps
skills.description: Follow a route or find a place on a neighbourhood map using a key, e.g. 'Which building is two blocks east of the park?'.

skills.name: How places connect
skills.description: Identify how people and goods move between places (roads, rail, ships, planes), e.g. pick the best way to send a letter across the sea long ago.

skills.name: Who leads what
skills.description: Match leaders to what they lead, e.g. mayor to town, governor or premier to a state or province, president or prime minister to a country.

skills.name: Voting to decide
skills.description: Understand that groups vote to make fair choices and count a simple tally to find the winner, e.g. 7 votes for pizza vs 5 for tacos.

skills.name: Why we have laws
skills.description: Explain what a law is for by picking which law solves a problem, e.g. a speed limit keeps people safe near schools.

skills.name: Cardinal directions
skills.description: Use north, south, east and west with a compass rose, e.g. 'The lake is ___ of the town'.

skills.name: Map key and title
skills.description: Use a map key to decode symbols and the title to know what the map shows, e.g. count the hospitals on a town map.

skills.name: Continents and oceans
skills.description: Name the seven continents and five oceans on a world map, e.g. tap Africa or pick the ocean between Americas and Europe.

skills.name: Producers and consumers
skills.description: Sort people in scenarios into producers (make or sell) and consumers (buy or use), e.g. a farmer vs a shopper.

skills.name: Money and exchange
skills.description: Recognise that money is traded for goods and services and compare simple prices, e.g. 'Which item costs more?'.

skills.name: Saving and spending
skills.description: Decide between saving and spending in a short story and compute simple savings, e.g. save 2 coins a week for 3 weeks.

skills.name: Technology then and now
skills.description: Order inventions or tools from oldest to newest, e.g. horse cart, steam train, car, electric car.

skills.name: People who made a difference
skills.description: Match historical figures from around the world to their contribution, e.g. a scientist to a discovery or a leader to a change they made.

skills.name: Daily life long ago
skills.description: Compare school, homes and play from long ago with today, e.g. 'Which was used to write at school 150 years ago?'.

skills.name: Celebrations around the world
skills.description: Match festivals such as Lunar New Year, Diwali, Eid and Carnival to a key feature or region, e.g. lanterns to Lunar New Year.

skills.name: Food, clothing and homes
skills.description: Link foods, clothes and house types to climate and place, e.g. choose why homes on stilts are built near rivers.

skills.name: Rights and responsibilities
skills.description: Sort statements into rights (what you may have) and responsibilities (what you should do), e.g. 'go to school' vs 'put litter in the bin'.

skills.name: Respecting differences
skills.description: Choose respectful responses to differences in a short scenario, e.g. a classmate speaks another language at home.

skills.name: Types of communities
skills.description: Compare how communities in different countries meet needs for food, water and shelter, e.g. pick why a desert town builds thick-walled houses.

skills.name: How communities change
skills.description: Identify causes of community change such as new roads, factories or migration, e.g. 'What happened after the railway arrived?'.

skills.name: Adapting to the environment
skills.description: Match ways people adapt to or change their environment, e.g. terraces on hillsides, dams, irrigation canals.

skills.name: Landforms and bodies of water
skills.description: Identify mountains, plains, plateaus, islands, peninsulas, rivers, lakes and bays from pictures or definitions, e.g. 'land surrounded by water on three sides'.

skills.name: Grids and scale
skills.description: Locate places with letter-number grid references and estimate distance with a bar scale, e.g. 'Which town is in square C4?'.

skills.name: Hemispheres, equator and poles
skills.description: Use the equator, prime meridian, hemispheres and poles to describe where a continent is, e.g. 'Australia is in which hemispheres?'.

skills.name: Local, state and national
skills.description: Sort services into local, regional and national government, e.g. trash pickup is local, the army is national.

skills.name: Who makes, carries out and judges laws
skills.description: Match the three jobs of government (make laws, carry out laws, decide if laws were broken) to simple examples, e.g. a judge decides a case.

skills.name: Citizens' rights and duties
skills.description: Identify basic rights (speech, worship, fair trial) and duties (obey laws, pay taxes, vote), e.g. choose which is a duty.

skills.name: Scarcity and choice
skills.description: Explain that limited resources force choices, e.g. with 5 coins choose what you can afford and what you give up.

skills.name: Natural, human and capital resources
skills.description: Sort inputs of a business into natural, human and capital resources, e.g. wood, carpenter, saw.

skills.name: Barter and money
skills.description: Compare bartering with using money and explain why money makes trade easier, e.g. choose the problem with trading a cow for bread.

skills.name: Reading timelines
skills.description: Place events on a timeline using years and decades and read how long between events, e.g. 'How many years from 1900 to 1950?'.

skills.name: Primary and secondary sources
skills.description: Sort sources into primary (diary, photo, letter) and secondary (textbook, encyclopedia), e.g. a soldier's letter is primary.

skills.name: First peoples of a region
skills.description: Identify how Indigenous peoples lived in a region before outsiders arrived, e.g. match a shelter type to its environment.

skills.name: Elements of culture
skills.description: Sort examples into language, religion, food, art, music and customs, e.g. a folk dance is art/music.

skills.name: Why people move
skills.description: Identify push and pull reasons people migrate, e.g. 'jobs in a new city' is a pull factor, 'war at home' is a push factor.

skills.name: Solving community problems
skills.description: Match a community problem to a reasonable civic action, e.g. unsafe crossing to 'ask the council for a crossing guard'.

skills.name: Volunteering and service
skills.description: Identify how volunteering helps a community and pick a suitable service project for a need, e.g. a food drive for hunger.

topics.name: Regions of a country and the world

skills.name: Regions of the United States
skills.description: Match states and features to the Northeast, Southeast, Midwest, Southwest and West, e.g. 'Texas is in which region?'.

skills.name: World regions
skills.description: Place countries in world regions such as Western Europe, East Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa or South America, e.g. 'Kenya is in...'.

skills.name: Climate and vegetation by region
skills.description: Link a region's climate to its vegetation and land use, e.g. match 'hot and dry' to desert scrub and ranching.

skills.name: Latitude and longitude
skills.description: Find a place from coordinates or give rough coordinates of a city, e.g. 'Which city is near 40N, 74W?'.

skills.name: Scale and distance
skills.description: Use a map scale to compute real distance, e.g. 3 cm on the map at 1 cm = 50 km is 150 km.

skills.name: Thematic maps
skills.description: Read population, rainfall, resource and elevation maps, e.g. 'Which area receives the most rain?'.

skills.name: Indigenous nations and regions
skills.description: Match Indigenous nations and culture groups to their regions and ways of life, e.g. Pueblo peoples to the Southwest and adobe homes.

skills.name: Environment shapes culture
skills.description: Explain how environment shaped food, shelter and tools of Indigenous groups, e.g. why Plains peoples followed bison.

skills.name: Explorers and routes
skills.description: Match European explorers to sponsoring country and route, e.g. Columbus to Spain and the Caribbean, Cabot to England.

skills.name: Motives and technology
skills.description: Identify reasons for exploration (gold, trade, religion) and tools that made it possible (compass, caravel, astrolabe).

skills.name: Effects of encounter
skills.description: Identify effects of European arrival on Indigenous peoples such as disease, trade and loss of land, e.g. choose the effect of smallpox.

topics.name: History of my state or region

skills.name: Settlement and growth
skills.description: Order the stages of a region's development from first peoples to statehood or modern times, e.g. sequence 4 milestones.

skills.name: Landmarks and symbols
skills.description: Identify a state or region's capital, flag, landmarks and symbols, e.g. 'Which city is the capital of California?'.

skills.name: What a constitution does
skills.description: Identify a constitution as the plan for government that limits power and protects rights, e.g. pick which statement describes its purpose.

skills.name: State and local government
skills.description: Match officials and bodies (governor, legislature, mayor, council) to their level and job, e.g. the governor leads the state executive.

skills.name: Ways citizens participate
skills.description: Identify ways to influence government such as voting, petitions, contacting representatives and peaceful protest, e.g. choose the best action for a new park.

skills.name: Supply and demand basics
skills.description: Predict whether price rises or falls when supply or demand changes, e.g. a frost ruins oranges so orange prices go up.

skills.name: Markets and prices
skills.description: Compare prices and compute totals and change for simple purchases, e.g. 3 items at 4 each with 20 paid.

skills.name: Taxes and public goods
skills.description: Sort goods into public (roads, parks, schools paid by taxes) and private, e.g. a streetlight vs a bicycle.

skills.name: Major physical features
skills.description: Locate the Rockies, Appalachians, Mississippi, Great Lakes, Great Plains and coasts on a map, e.g. tap the Great Lakes.

skills.name: States, provinces and capitals
skills.description: Match states or provinces to capitals and locations, e.g. Illinois to Springfield, Ontario to Toronto.

skills.name: Where people live and why
skills.description: Explain why cities grow near rivers, coasts and resources, e.g. choose why New Orleans sits at a river mouth.

skills.name: The thirteen colonies
skills.description: Sort colonies into New England, Middle and Southern regions and match them to economies, e.g. Virginia to tobacco plantations.

skills.name: Colonial daily life
skills.description: Describe life for farmers, artisans, enslaved people and Indigenous neighbours in the colonies, e.g. choose who worked in the triangular-trade economy without pay.

skills.name: Atlantic trade and slavery
skills.description: Trace the routes and goods of the triangular trade and the Middle Passage, e.g. sequence the legs of the trade.

skills.name: Causes of the Revolution
skills.description: Order and explain events from the Stamp Act to Lexington, e.g. sequence Stamp Act, Boston Tea Party, First Continental Congress.

skills.name: The Declaration of Independence
skills.description: Identify key ideas (rights, consent of the governed) and facts (1776, Jefferson) of the Declaration, e.g. choose what 'unalienable rights' means.

skills.name: Battles and leaders
skills.description: Match key battles and people (Saratoga, Yorktown, Washington, Lafayette) to their role, e.g. Yorktown to the final British surrender.

skills.name: Articles of Confederation
skills.description: Identify weaknesses of the Articles (no power to tax, no national army) that led to a new constitution, e.g. choose a problem the Articles caused.

skills.name: Convention compromises
skills.description: Match the Great Compromise and Three-Fifths Compromise to the dispute they settled, e.g. representation of big vs small states.

skills.name: The Bill of Rights
skills.description: Match the first ten amendments to the rights they protect, e.g. the First Amendment to free speech and religion.

skills.name: Louisiana Purchase and Lewis and Clark
skills.description: Explain the 1803 purchase and the expedition it prompted, e.g. choose how much US land roughly doubled.

skills.name: Trails and pioneers
skills.description: Match trails and events (Oregon Trail, Gold Rush, Erie Canal) to places and effects, e.g. the Gold Rush to California 1849.

skills.name: Impact on Indigenous nations
skills.description: Identify the Indian Removal Act and Trail of Tears and their consequences, e.g. choose which nation was forced from Georgia.

skills.name: Opportunity cost basics
skills.description: Name the next-best thing given up in a choice, e.g. buying a game instead of a book means the book is the opportunity cost.

skills.name: Budgets and saving
skills.description: Build a simple budget and compute what remains after spending, e.g. income 50, spending 35, saving is 15.

skills.name: Specialisation and interdependence
skills.description: Explain why regions specialise and trade, e.g. choose why a fishing town buys wheat instead of growing it.

skills.name: World cultures and religions
skills.description: Match major world religions and cultural regions to key features and places, e.g. Buddhism to its origin in India.

skills.name: Global exchange of goods and ideas
skills.description: Identify goods and ideas that crossed the world (potatoes, horses, printing, numerals) and their origin, e.g. potatoes came from the Andes.

skills.name: Identify ancient civilizations
skills.description: Match civilizations (Mesopotamia, Egypt, Indus, Shang China, Olmec) to their river, region and signature achievement, e.g. cuneiform to Mesopotamia.

skills.name: Why civilizations grew by rivers
skills.description: Explain how rivers enabled farming, surplus and cities, e.g. choose why the Nile flood was good for farmers.

skills.name: Inventions and achievements
skills.description: Match inventions such as the wheel, writing, the calendar, paper and bronze to the civilization that developed them.

skills.name: Beliefs and social structure
skills.description: Identify religious beliefs and social classes of early societies, e.g. order Egyptian society from pharaoh to enslaved people.

skills.name: Physical geography of the ancient world
skills.description: Locate rivers, seas, deserts and mountain ranges (Nile, Tigris, Mediterranean, Sahara, Himalayas) and explain how they shaped settlement, e.g. tap the Fertile Crescent.

skills.name: Human geography
skills.description: Identify how people use land, settle and build, e.g. choose why most Egyptians lived in a narrow strip along the Nile.

skills.name: Map types and projections
skills.description: Choose the right map (political, physical, historical) for a question and recognise that projections distort size, e.g. Greenland looks larger than it is.

skills.name: Chronology and eras
skills.description: Order events and civilizations on a BCE/CE timeline and compute spans, e.g. sequence Sumer, Old Kingdom Egypt, Classical Athens, Han China.

skills.name: Sources and evidence
skills.description: Decide what an artifact or text can and cannot tell us and whether it is primary or secondary, e.g. a Roman coin shows an emperor's face but not his thoughts.

skills.name: Cause and effect
skills.description: Link a historical cause to its effect, e.g. irrigation leads to surplus leads to cities and specialised jobs.

skills.name: Ancient Greece
skills.description: Identify Greek city-states, Athenian democracy, philosophers and the Persian and Peloponnesian wars, e.g. choose what Athenian citizens did in the Assembly.

skills.name: Ancient Rome
skills.description: Sequence Rome from republic to empire to fall and match features such as the Senate, Twelve Tables and aqueducts, e.g. order Republic, Augustus, Pax Romana, fall of the West.

skills.name: Classical India and China
skills.description: Match the Maurya and Gupta empires and the Qin and Han dynasties to achievements such as the Great Wall, civil service, zero and Buddhism's spread.

skills.name: From barter to coins
skills.description: Explain why societies moved from barter to standard money, e.g. choose the problem coins solved for merchants in Lydia.

skills.name: Surplus and specialisation
skills.description: Explain how food surplus allowed scribes, priests and artisans, e.g. sequence farming surplus to job specialisation to social classes.

skills.name: Early trade networks
skills.description: Match goods and ideas to the Silk Road, Indian Ocean and Mediterranean routes, e.g. silk flows west, glass and horses flow east.

skills.name: City-states, kingdoms, empires
skills.description: Sort examples into city-state, kingdom and empire and explain the difference, e.g. Athens vs Persia.

skills.name: Early law codes
skills.description: Identify Hammurabi's Code and the Roman Twelve Tables and what written law changed, e.g. choose a principle from Hammurabi's Code.

skills.name: Origins of democracy and republic
skills.description: Compare Athenian direct democracy with the Roman Republic, e.g. sort features such as 'citizens vote on laws directly' vs 'elected senators'.

skills.name: Writing systems
skills.description: Match cuneiform, hieroglyphs, the Phoenician alphabet and Chinese characters to their civilizations and purposes.

skills.name: Art and architecture
skills.description: Identify pyramids, ziggurats, the Parthenon, the Colosseum and other monuments by civilization, e.g. a ziggurat is Mesopotamian.

skills.name: Legacies in the modern world
skills.description: Link modern things (alphabet, calendar, democracy, concrete, the Olympics) to their ancient origin, e.g. the Olympics to Greece.

skills.name: Feudalism and manor life
skills.description: Order the feudal hierarchy and match roles, e.g. sequence king, lords, knights, peasants and serfs.

skills.name: The Church and Byzantium
skills.description: Identify the role of the medieval Church, the Byzantine Empire and Justinian's Code, e.g. choose Constantinople's importance.

skills.name: Crusades, plague and change
skills.description: Explain causes and effects of the Crusades, the Black Death and the Magna Carta, e.g. choose how the plague changed workers' wages.

skills.name: The Islamic world
skills.description: Identify the rise and spread of Islam and achievements of the Islamic Golden Age (algebra, medicine, Baghdad's House of Wisdom), e.g. match a scholar to a field.

skills.name: African kingdoms
skills.description: Match Ghana, Mali, Songhai, Axum and Great Zimbabwe to locations, trade goods and leaders, e.g. Mansa Musa to Mali and gold.

skills.name: China, Japan and the Mongols
skills.description: Identify Tang/Song inventions, Japanese feudalism (shogun, samurai) and the Mongol Empire's extent and effects, e.g. choose a Song dynasty invention.

skills.name: Maya, Aztec and Inca
skills.description: Match the three civilizations to regions, capitals and achievements, e.g. Inca to the Andes and road network, Maya to calendar and glyphs.

skills.name: North American societies
skills.description: Identify Mississippian mound builders, Ancestral Puebloans and other societies and how environment shaped them, e.g. Cahokia to the Mississippi valley.

skills.name: Renaissance ideas and art
skills.description: Identify humanism, patronage and key figures (Leonardo, Michelangelo, Gutenberg), e.g. choose the effect of the printing press.

skills.name: The Reformation
skills.description: Explain Luther's 95 Theses, the split in Western Christianity and the Counter-Reformation, e.g. sequence 1517 Theses, Protestant churches, Council of Trent.

skills.name: The Scientific Revolution
skills.description: Match Copernicus, Galileo and Newton to their ideas and explain the scientific method, e.g. heliocentrism to Copernicus.

skills.name: Age of Exploration
skills.description: Match explorers and empires (Portugal, Spain, Ming treasure fleets) to routes and goals, e.g. da Gama to the sea route to India.

skills.name: The Columbian Exchange
skills.description: Sort plants, animals and diseases by whether they crossed from the Americas or to the Americas, e.g. maize went east, horses went west.

skills.name: Colonial empires and slavery
skills.description: Identify Spanish, Portuguese and other colonial systems and the Atlantic slave trade's scale and effects, e.g. choose what the encomienda system was.

skills.name: Climate regions and biomes
skills.description: Match climate zones (tropical, arid, temperate, continental, polar) and biomes to regions and explain how latitude and altitude shape them, e.g. the Sahara is arid.

skills.name: Population patterns
skills.description: Read population density maps and explain why people cluster, e.g. choose why northern India and eastern China are densely settled.

skills.name: Resources and regions
skills.description: Match regions to key natural resources and the activities they support, e.g. the Persian Gulf to oil, the Pampas to cattle.

skills.name: Types of government
skills.description: Classify historical and modern states as monarchy, theocracy, oligarchy, democracy, republic or dictatorship from a description, e.g. 'rule by religious leaders' is a theocracy.

skills.name: Rule of law and limits on power
skills.description: Identify documents and ideas that limited rulers (Magna Carta, Justinian's Code, English Parliament), e.g. choose what Magna Carta forced the king to accept.

skills.name: Citizenship across time
skills.description: Compare who counted as a citizen in Athens, Rome, medieval towns and today, e.g. sort groups by whether they could vote in Athens.

skills.name: Trade routes and exchange
skills.description: Match trade routes (Silk Road, trans-Saharan, Indian Ocean, Hanseatic League) to goods traded and the cities they enriched, e.g. salt and gold crossed the Sahara via Timbuktu.

skills.name: Mercantilism and colonies
skills.description: Explain how colonies supplied raw materials and bought finished goods to enrich the home country, e.g. choose the mercantilist view of gold.

skills.name: Traditional, command and market systems
skills.description: Classify how a society answers what to produce and who gets it, e.g. 'custom decides' is traditional, 'the ruler decides' is command.

skills.name: Colonial regions and economies
skills.description: Compare New England, Middle and Southern colonies by economy, labour and religion, e.g. choose which region relied most on enslaved labour.

skills.name: Roots of self-government
skills.description: Identify the Mayflower Compact, House of Burgesses, town meetings and English rights as origins of American self-rule, e.g. match each to its colony.

skills.name: Enlightenment influences
skills.description: Match Locke, Montesquieu and Rousseau to natural rights, separation of powers and the social contract, e.g. 'life, liberty, property' to Locke.

skills.name: Road to revolution
skills.description: Sequence and explain British policies and colonial responses 1763-1775, e.g. order Proclamation of 1763, Stamp Act, Boston Massacre, Intolerable Acts.

skills.name: Winning the war
skills.description: Explain turning points and advantages (Saratoga and French alliance, Valley Forge, Yorktown, Treaty of Paris 1783), e.g. choose why Saratoga mattered.

skills.name: Founding documents
skills.description: Identify purpose and key passages of the Declaration, Articles of Confederation and Constitution, e.g. match 'We the People' to the Preamble.

skills.name: Separation of powers and checks
