skills.description: Match powers to Congress, the President or the courts and identify checks, e.g. a veto is an executive check on Congress.

skills.name: Federalism
skills.description: Sort powers into national, state and shared, e.g. coining money is national, schools are state, taxing is shared.

skills.name: Federalists vs Anti-Federalists
skills.description: Classify arguments as Federalist or Anti-Federalist and explain the Bill of Rights compromise, e.g. 'a strong central government threatens liberty' is Anti-Federalist.

skills.name: Amending the Constitution
skills.description: Sequence the amendment process and identify key amendments 1-10, 13, 14, 15, 19, e.g. order proposal by two-thirds of Congress then ratification by three-fourths of states.

skills.name: Washington and Adams
skills.description: Identify precedents and crises of the first presidencies (cabinet, Hamilton's bank, Whiskey Rebellion, Farewell Address), e.g. choose Washington's advice about alliances.

skills.name: Jefferson, Marshall and expansion
skills.description: Explain the Louisiana Purchase, Marbury v. Madison and judicial review, e.g. choose what power Marbury established.

skills.name: War of 1812 and nationalism
skills.description: Identify causes and effects of the War of 1812 and the Monroe Doctrine, e.g. choose an effect of the war on US manufacturing.

skills.name: Manifest Destiny
skills.description: Sequence territorial gains (Texas, Oregon, Mexican Cession, Gadsden) and evaluate their causes and costs, e.g. order annexations by year.

skills.name: Early industrialisation
skills.description: Identify inventions (cotton gin, steamboat, telegraph) and their economic effects, e.g. choose how the cotton gin affected slavery.

skills.name: Reform movements
skills.description: Match abolition, women's rights (Seneca Falls), temperance and education reform to leaders and goals, e.g. Frederick Douglass to abolition.

skills.name: Compromises and sectional crisis
skills.description: Sequence the Missouri Compromise, Compromise of 1850, Kansas-Nebraska Act, Dred Scott and Lincoln's election, e.g. order the five events.

skills.name: Course of the war
skills.description: Match key events and documents (Fort Sumter, Antietam, Emancipation Proclamation, Gettysburg, Appomattox) to significance, e.g. Gettysburg to the turning point in the East.

skills.name: Reconstruction
skills.description: Identify the 13th-15th Amendments, Freedmen's Bureau, Black Codes and the Compromise of 1877, e.g. choose what the 14th Amendment guaranteed.

skills.name: Rights and duties of citizens
skills.description: Distinguish rights, duties and responsibilities and explain naturalisation, e.g. jury service is a duty, voting is a responsibility.

skills.name: Landmark Supreme Court cases
skills.description: Match cases (Marbury, McCulloch, Dred Scott, Plessy) to the principle they set, e.g. McCulloch to implied powers.

skills.name: How a bill becomes law
skills.description: Sequence the steps from introduction through committee, floor votes, conference and presidential action, e.g. order 6 steps.

skills.name: Market economy and growth
skills.description: Explain how markets, banks, canals and railroads expanded the economy, e.g. choose how the Erie Canal changed grain prices in New York.

skills.name: Tariffs and sectional interests
skills.description: Explain why the North favoured tariffs and the South opposed them and compute a simple tariff, e.g. 25 percent on a 40 dollar import.

skills.name: Five themes of geography
skills.description: Classify statements as location, place, human-environment interaction, movement or region, e.g. 'Dutch dikes hold back the sea' is human-environment interaction.

skills.name: Physical systems
skills.description: Explain plate tectonics, climate drivers, ocean currents and biomes, e.g. choose why the west coast of South America is dry.

skills.name: Human-environment interaction
skills.description: Evaluate how people adapt to and alter environments (irrigation, deforestation, urban heat), e.g. identify the cause of the Aral Sea shrinking.

skills.name: Demographic patterns
skills.description: Read population pyramids and compute growth from birth and death rates, e.g. birth rate 30 and death rate 10 per 1000 gives 2 percent growth.

skills.name: Migration
skills.description: Classify push and pull factors and types of migration (voluntary, forced, refugee, internal), e.g. drought is a push factor.

skills.name: Cultural diffusion and regions
skills.description: Identify how languages, religions and customs spread and map culture regions, e.g. choose how Spanish became dominant in Latin America.

skills.name: States, nations and sovereignty
skills.description: Distinguish state, nation, nation-state and stateless nation with examples, e.g. the Kurds are a stateless nation.

skills.name: Borders and conflict
skills.description: Classify boundary types and identify causes of border disputes, e.g. the 49th parallel is a geometric boundary.

skills.name: International organisations
skills.description: Match the UN, EU, NATO, African Union and WTO to purpose and membership, e.g. NATO to collective defence.

skills.name: Measuring development
skills.description: Interpret GDP per capita, HDI, literacy and life expectancy to compare countries, e.g. rank three countries by HDI.

skills.name: Economic sectors
skills.description: Sort jobs into primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors and link sector mix to development, e.g. mining is primary.

skills.name: Globalisation and supply chains
skills.description: Trace a product's supply chain and identify winners and losers of globalisation, e.g. sequence design, component manufacture, assembly, retail across countries.

skills.name: Resources and energy
skills.description: Classify renewable and non-renewable resources and read energy-mix charts, e.g. choose which country relies most on hydropower.

skills.name: Europe and Russia
skills.description: Locate countries and capitals and explain key regional issues (EU integration, energy dependence), e.g. tap Poland on a map.

skills.name: Asia and the Pacific
skills.description: Locate major countries, rivers and cities and explain monsoon, megacities and economic rise, e.g. match the Ganges to India and Bangladesh.

skills.name: Africa and the Middle East
skills.description: Locate countries and features (Sahel, Nile, Gulf) and explain colonial borders, oil and water issues, e.g. choose why many African borders are straight lines.

skills.name: Latin America and the Caribbean
skills.description: Locate countries, the Andes and Amazon and explain urbanisation and colonial legacies, e.g. match Brazil to Portuguese.

skills.name: Industrialisation spreads
skills.description: Explain why industrialisation began in Britain and how it spread to Europe, the US and Japan, e.g. choose a British advantage such as coal.

skills.name: Imperialism and its legacy
skills.description: Map 19th-century empires and link them to today's languages and borders, e.g. match a former colony to its colonial power.

skills.name: Nationalism and unification
skills.description: Identify how nationalism created Italy and Germany and strained empires, e.g. choose Bismarck's role.

skills.name: GIS, GPS and remote sensing
skills.description: Choose the right tool and map layer for a question, e.g. use satellite images to track deforestation over time.

skills.name: Reading data maps and graphs
skills.description: Interpret choropleth maps, cartograms and scatter plots and spot misleading scales, e.g. choose what a darker shade means on a choropleth.

skills.name: Enlightenment political thought
skills.description: Match thinkers to ideas and trace them into revolutions, e.g. Montesquieu's separation of powers to the US Constitution.

skills.name: French Revolution and Napoleon
skills.description: Sequence phases from the Estates-General to Napoleon's defeat and explain causes, e.g. order 1789, Terror, Directory, Empire, Waterloo.

skills.name: Latin American and Haitian independence
skills.description: Match leaders (Toussaint Louverture, Bolivar, Hidalgo) to movements and explain shared causes, e.g. Haiti as the first successful slave revolution.

skills.name: Industrial society
skills.description: Identify changes in work, cities and class and the ideologies (capitalism, socialism, Marxism) that responded, e.g. match Marx to class struggle.

skills.name: Labour and reform
skills.description: Explain unions, child labour laws and suffrage movements as responses to industrialisation, e.g. choose the goal of the Factory Acts.

skills.name: Demographic and urban change
skills.description: Interpret data on urbanisation and population growth 1750-1900, e.g. compute percent growth of a city from 100,000 to 250,000.

skills.name: Motives and methods of imperialism
skills.description: Classify motives (economic, strategic, ideological) and forms of control (colony, protectorate, sphere of influence), e.g. Egypt under Britain was a protectorate.

skills.name: Partition of Africa and Asia
skills.description: Match the Berlin Conference, Opium Wars, Raj and Meiji response to effects, e.g. choose how Japan avoided colonisation.

skills.name: Resistance and nationalism
skills.description: Identify resistance (Sepoy Rebellion, Boxer Uprising, Ethiopian victory at Adwa) and early nationalist movements, e.g. match Adwa to Ethiopia.

skills.name: World War I
skills.description: Explain MAIN causes, trench stalemate and the Versailles settlement, e.g. choose a Versailles term that fuelled German resentment.

skills.name: Interwar crisis and totalitarianism
skills.description: Link the Depression and Versailles to fascism, Nazism and Stalinism and compare the regimes, e.g. sort traits of totalitarian states.

skills.name: World War II and the Holocaust
skills.description: Sequence key events (invasion of Poland, Pearl Harbor, Stalingrad, D-Day, Hiroshima) and explain the Holocaust and its aftermath, e.g. choose what the Nuremberg trials established.

skills.name: Superpower rivalry
skills.description: Explain containment, NATO vs Warsaw Pact, the arms race and detente, e.g. match the Berlin Airlift to containment.

skills.name: Proxy conflicts
skills.description: Match Korea, Vietnam, Cuba, Afghanistan and Angola to superpower involvement and outcome, e.g. the Cuban Missile Crisis to 1962.

skills.name: Decolonisation
skills.description: Match independence leaders and movements (Gandhi, Nkrumah, Ho Chi Minh, Mandela) to countries and methods, e.g. Ghana to 1957 and Nkrumah.

skills.name: End of the Cold War
skills.description: Sequence Gorbachev's reforms, the fall of the Berlin Wall and the Soviet collapse and explain causes, e.g. order glasnost, 1989, 1991.

skills.name: Globalisation and technology
skills.description: Evaluate effects of the internet, container shipping and multinational firms, e.g. choose an effect of container shipping on prices.

skills.name: Human rights and genocide
skills.description: Identify the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the Genocide Convention and cases (Rwanda, Bosnia), e.g. choose what the UDHR is.

skills.name: Global challenges
skills.description: Explain climate change, pandemics, terrorism and migration as global issues requiring cooperation, e.g. match the Paris Agreement to its goal.

skills.name: Sourcing and corroboration
skills.description: Evaluate a source's author, purpose, audience and reliability and check it against another, e.g. choose why a propaganda poster is still useful evidence.

skills.name: Perspective and interpretation
skills.description: Recognise how historians' interpretations differ and identify the perspective in a passage, e.g. decide whether an account is colonial or anti-colonial.

skills.name: Continuity and change
skills.description: Identify what changed and what stayed the same across a period, e.g. sort features of 1900 vs 2000 Europe into changed or continuous.

skills.name: Comparing economic systems
skills.description: Compare capitalism, socialism, communism and mixed economies on ownership and decision-making, e.g. sort traits of a command economy.

skills.name: Global economic institutions
skills.description: Match the IMF, World Bank, WTO and Bretton Woods to purpose, e.g. the World Bank to development loans.

skills.name: Constitutional principles in practice
skills.description: Apply popular sovereignty, limited government, federalism and checks and balances to historical cases, e.g. identify which principle the Alien and Sedition Acts tested.

skills.name: Early party politics
skills.description: Compare Federalist and Democratic-Republican positions and trace the growth of democracy under Jackson, e.g. sort positions on the national bank.

topics.name: Civil War and Reconstruction in depth

skills.name: Causes and course
skills.description: Analyse slavery, states' rights and economic differences as causes and interpret Lincoln's speeches, e.g. choose the main argument of the Gettysburg Address.

skills.name: Reconstruction and its end
skills.description: Evaluate Reconstruction's successes and failures, Jim Crow and Plessy v. Ferguson, e.g. choose how sharecropping limited freedom.

skills.name: Industrialisation and immigration
skills.description: Explain big business, monopolies, urban growth and new immigration 1870-1920, e.g. match Carnegie to steel and vertical integration.

skills.name: Labour movements
skills.description: Identify strikes, unions and outcomes (Haymarket, Pullman, AFL), e.g. choose why the Pullman strike failed.

skills.name: Progressive reforms
skills.description: Match reforms and amendments (16th-19th, Pure Food and Drug Act, trust-busting) to problems they addressed, e.g. the 17th Amendment to Senate elections.

skills.name: The West and Indigenous nations
skills.description: Explain homesteading, railroads, the Dawes Act and Wounded Knee, e.g. choose the purpose of the Dawes Act.

skills.name: US overseas expansion
skills.description: Explain the Spanish-American War, Hawaii, the Philippines and the Panama Canal and debate imperialism, e.g. sort arguments for and against annexing the Philippines.

skills.name: World War I and the home front
skills.description: Explain US entry, mobilisation, civil liberties limits and the League debate, e.g. choose why the Senate rejected the Treaty of Versailles.

skills.name: 1920s society and culture
skills.description: Identify the Harlem Renaissance, consumer culture, Prohibition and nativism, e.g. match Langston Hughes to the Harlem Renaissance.

skills.name: Causes of the Great Depression
skills.description: Explain speculation, bank failures, overproduction and tariffs as causes and read unemployment data, e.g. choose the effect of the Smoot-Hawley tariff.

skills.name: The New Deal
skills.description: Classify New Deal programs as relief, recovery or reform and evaluate critics, e.g. Social Security is reform, the CCC is relief.

topics.name: World War II and Cold War America

skills.name: World War II at home and abroad
skills.description: Explain mobilisation, Japanese American internment, D-Day, the atomic bomb decision and the UN, e.g. choose what Korematsu v. US ruled.

skills.name: Cold War policy
skills.description: Explain containment, the Marshall Plan, McCarthyism, Korea and the space race, e.g. match the Truman Doctrine to aid for Greece and Turkey.

skills.name: Civil rights movement
skills.description: Sequence Brown v. Board, Montgomery, Little Rock, the March on Washington, the Civil Rights Act and Voting Rights Act and match leaders to strategies, e.g. order the six events.

skills.name: Vietnam, protest and Watergate
skills.description: Explain escalation, the antiwar and counterculture movements and Watergate's effect on trust in government, e.g. choose what the War Powers Act did.

skills.name: Conservative resurgence
skills.description: Identify Reagan-era policies (tax cuts, deregulation, defence buildup) and their effects, e.g. choose a goal of supply-side economics.

skills.name: Post-Cold War America
skills.description: Identify the Gulf War, 9/11 and its wars, the 2008 financial crisis and technological change, e.g. sequence 1991, 2001, 2008.

skills.name: Supply and demand
skills.description: Predict the effect of a shift in supply or demand on equilibrium price and quantity and read it off a chart, e.g. a rise in input costs shifts supply left so price rises and quantity falls.

skills.name: Elasticity
skills.description: Compute price elasticity of demand from percent changes and classify as elastic or inelastic, e.g. quantity falls 20 percent when price rises 10 percent gives elasticity 2, elastic.

skills.name: Opportunity cost and trade-offs
skills.description: Identify the opportunity cost of a decision and use a production possibilities frontier, e.g. producing 10 more cars costs 5 trucks.

skills.name: Incentives and market roles
skills.description: Explain how prices, profits and incentives coordinate producers and consumers and identify market failures, e.g. choose why a price ceiling causes shortages.

skills.name: Political theory and democracy models
skills.description: Match theorists and models (Hobbes, Locke, pluralist, elite, participatory democracy) to claims, e.g. 'competing groups shape policy' is pluralist.

skills.name: Analysing the Constitution
skills.description: Locate powers and clauses (necessary and proper, commerce, supremacy) and apply them to cases, e.g. choose which clause McCulloch v. Maryland relied on.

skills.name: Federalism today
skills.description: Classify grants, mandates and devolution and analyse federal-state conflicts, e.g. a block grant gives states more discretion than a categorical grant.

skills.name: Congress
skills.description: Explain committees, leadership, filibuster, reapportionment and the legislative process, e.g. compute the votes needed to end a filibuster in a 100-seat Senate.

skills.name: Presidency and bureaucracy
skills.description: Identify formal and informal presidential powers and how agencies make rules, e.g. an executive order is an informal power.

skills.name: The judiciary
skills.description: Explain judicial review, jurisdiction, precedent and judicial activism vs restraint, e.g. sequence a case from district court to Supreme Court.

skills.name: First Amendment cases
skills.description: Apply precedents (Tinker, Schenck, Engel, New York Times v. US) to scenarios, e.g. decide whether a school may ban a political armband.

skills.name: Due process and incorporation
skills.description: Explain selective incorporation and criminal-procedure rights (Gideon, Miranda, Mapp), e.g. match Miranda to the right to be told of rights.

skills.name: Equal protection and civil rights law
skills.description: Apply the 14th Amendment, Brown, the Civil Rights Act, Title IX and affirmative action cases, e.g. choose the standard of scrutiny for race-based classifications.

skills.name: Elections and voting
skills.description: Explain the Electoral College, primaries, turnout factors and voting rights laws, e.g. compute electoral votes needed to win from 538.

skills.name: Parties, interest groups and PACs
skills.description: Distinguish party functions, interest group tactics and campaign finance rules, e.g. lobbying vs litigation vs grassroots.

skills.name: Media and public opinion
skills.description: Interpret polls (sample, margin of error) and identify media effects and bias, e.g. a result of 52 percent with margin 3 is a statistical tie with 48.

skills.name: Comparing political systems
skills.description: Compare presidential vs parliamentary systems, federal vs unitary states and authoritarian regimes, e.g. the UK is parliamentary and unitary.

skills.name: International relations
skills.description: Explain foreign policy tools, the UN Security Council, treaties and alliances, e.g. choose which body can authorise sanctions.

skills.name: Inflation and interest rates
