topics.name: Spanish vocabulary: routines, shopping and celebrations

skills.name: Daily routine and personal care
skills.description: Order a morning routine from 'despertarse' to 'salir de casa' and match items like 'el cepillo de dientes'.

skills.name: Clothing, sizes and shopping
skills.description: Match descriptions such as 'una falda de rayas, talla mediana' to pictures and complete a store dialogue.

skills.name: Celebrations and life events
skills.description: Sort vocabulary such as 'la boda', 'el cumpleanos', 'la quinceanera' with associated items and actions.

topics.name: Spanish reading: narratives in the past

skills.name: Stories told in the past
skills.description: Read a short narrative in the preterite and order the events or answer what happened first.

skills.name: Short biographies
skills.description: Read a short biography of a figure like Frida Kahlo and pull out dates and achievements.

skills.name: Recounting a weekend
skills.description: Listen to someone describe what they did last weekend and pick the activities in order.

skills.name: Short interviews
skills.description: Listen to a brief interview and identify the speaker's routine, preferences or plans.

skills.name: Writing about the past
skills.description: Assemble a five-sentence paragraph about yesterday using connectors like 'primero', 'luego', 'finalmente'.

skills.name: Editing for agreement and tense
skills.description: Spot and fix the error in a sentence, e.g. 'Ayer yo como pizza' should be 'comi'.

skills.name: Festivals across the Spanish-speaking world
skills.description: Match festivals such as La Tomatina, Inti Raymi and Carnaval de Barranquilla to countries and dates.

skills.name: Regional cuisine
skills.description: Match dishes like ceviche, arepas and tortilla espanola to their countries and main ingredients.

skills.name: Hispanic communities worldwide
skills.description: Answer facts about Spanish speakers in the United States and other countries, e.g. which US states have the most speakers.

skills.name: Imperfect tense
skills.description: Conjugate the imperfect, including ir, ser and ver, e.g. 'jugabamos', 'eran', 'veia', to describe habits in the past.

skills.name: Preterite versus imperfect
skills.description: Choose the tense for each verb in a story, e.g. 'Llovia (imperfect) cuando sali (preterite) de casa', and sort trigger words.

skills.name: Future tense
skills.description: Form the simple future, including irregular stems, e.g. 'viajare', 'tendran', 'haremos'.

skills.name: Formal and nosotros commands
skills.description: Form usted/ustedes commands and 'vamos a' or nosotros commands, e.g. 'Hable mas despacio', 'Comamos'.

topics.name: Spanish grammar: double pronouns and impersonal se

skills.name: Double object pronouns
skills.description: Combine indirect and direct pronouns, changing le to se, e.g. 'Se lo di' for 'Le di el libro a Juan'.

skills.name: Impersonal and passive se
skills.description: Complete signs and statements like 'Se habla espanol' and 'Se venden casas', choosing singular or plural.

skills.name: Adverbs and -mente
skills.description: Form adverbs from adjectives, e.g. 'rapida' to 'rapidamente', and place them in a sentence.

topics.name: Spanish vocabulary: environment, technology and work

skills.name: Environment and nature
skills.description: Sort words such as 'la contaminacion', 'reciclar', 'la selva' into problems, solutions and places.

skills.name: Technology and media
skills.description: Match terms like 'la pantalla', 'descargar', 'la red social' to definitions or icons.

skills.name: Professions and workplaces
skills.description: Match jobs such as 'la enfermera' and 'el ingeniero' to workplaces and tasks.

skills.name: Simplified news articles
skills.description: Read a short article and identify the main idea, a supporting detail and the author's purpose.

skills.name: Legends and folktales
skills.description: Read a legend such as La Llorona or El Dorado and sequence the plot or identify the moral.

skills.name: Infographics and data
skills.description: Read a Spanish infographic about recycling or screen time and extract numbers and comparisons.

skills.name: Talking about childhood
skills.description: Answer 'Que hacias cuando eras nino?' with imperfect sentences, e.g. 'Jugaba en el parque todos los dias'.

skills.name: Discussing future plans
skills.description: Build answers to 'Que haras el proximo verano?' using the future tense and time markers.

skills.name: At a restaurant
skills.description: Sequence a full restaurant exchange from being seated to paying, picking appropriate lines for each step.

skills.name: Narrating with two past tenses
skills.description: Assemble a story paragraph that uses imperfect for background and preterite for events in the right places.

skills.name: Transitions and connectors
skills.description: Choose connectors such as 'sin embargo', 'por eso', 'ademas' to link two sentences logically.

skills.name: Maya, Aztec and Inca
skills.description: Match achievements such as the Maya calendar, Tenochtitlan and Inca roads to the right civilization and region.

skills.name: Colonial era and independence
skills.description: Order key events from 1492 to the independence movements and match leaders such as Bolivar and Hidalgo to countries.

skills.name: Art and muralism
skills.description: Match artists such as Diego Rivera, Frida Kahlo and Fernando Botero to their styles and works.

topics.name: Spanish verbs: conditional, perfect and subjunctive

skills.name: Conditional tense
skills.description: Form the conditional, including irregular stems, e.g. 'me gustaria', 'podrias', 'harian', for polite requests and hypotheticals.

skills.name: Present perfect
skills.description: Combine haber with the past participle, including irregulars, e.g. 'he visto', 'hemos escrito'.

skills.name: Present subjunctive forms
skills.description: Conjugate the present subjunctive from the yo stem, including irregulars like sea, vaya, tenga and spelling changes.

skills.name: Subjunctive after wishes, emotions and doubt
skills.description: Choose indicative or subjunctive after triggers, e.g. 'Quiero que vengas' versus 'Se que vienes', and sort WEIRDO triggers.

topics.name: Spanish grammar: por/para, relatives and verbs like gustar

skills.name: Por versus para
skills.description: Choose por or para by meaning, e.g. 'Gracias por la ayuda' and 'Este regalo es para ti', and sort uses by rule.

skills.name: Relative pronouns
skills.description: Join two sentences with que, quien, lo que or donde, e.g. 'La chica que canta es mi prima'.

skills.name: Verbs like gustar
skills.description: Use faltar, importar, molestar, parecer with indirect pronouns and agreement, e.g. 'Nos faltan dos sillas'.

topics.name: Spanish vocabulary: society and global issues

skills.name: Community and volunteering
skills.description: Match words such as 'el voluntariado', 'donar', 'el refugio' to definitions and scenarios.

skills.name: Health and wellbeing
skills.description: Sort advice such as 'hacer ejercicio' and 'dormir ocho horas' into physical and mental health, and match symptoms to remedies.

skills.name: Idioms and expressions
skills.description: Match idioms such as 'estar en las nubes' or 'tomar el pelo' to their meanings.

skills.name: Authentic news and opinion
skills.description: Read an excerpt from a real newspaper or blog and distinguish fact from opinion and identify tone.

skills.name: Short fiction excerpts
skills.description: Read a passage from a short story and answer questions about character motivation and inference.

skills.name: Poetry
skills.description: Read a short poem by a poet such as Neruda or Mistral and identify imagery, theme and a figure of speech.

skills.name: Giving advice and recommendations
skills.description: Build advice with 'te recomiendo que' + subjunctive or 'deberias' + infinitive for a given situation.

skills.name: Expressing and supporting opinions
skills.description: Choose phrases like 'Creo que', 'No creo que' and the correct mood that follows each to state an opinion.

skills.name: Talking about what you would do
skills.description: Answer 'Que harias con un millon de dolares?' using the conditional in a complete sentence.

skills.name: Formal letters and emails
skills.description: Order the parts of a formal email and pick register-appropriate phrases such as 'Estimado senor' and 'Atentamente'.

skills.name: Summarizing a text
skills.description: Choose the sentence that best summarizes a paragraph without adding or distorting information.

skills.name: Literary figures
skills.description: Match authors such as Cervantes, Garcia Marquez, Allende and Borges to countries and major works.

skills.name: Music genres and origins
skills.description: Match genres such as reggaeton, cumbia, bachata and flamenco to their origins and instruments.

skills.name: Regional varieties of Spanish
skills.description: Identify features like vosotros, voseo and seseo and match regional words, e.g. 'guagua' for bus in the Caribbean.

topics.name: Spanish verbs: advanced subjunctive and compound tenses

skills.name: Imperfect subjunctive
skills.description: Form the imperfect subjunctive from the ellos preterite, e.g. 'hablara', 'tuvieran', 'fueramos', after past triggers.

skills.name: Si clauses
skills.description: Complete hypothetical sentences pairing imperfect subjunctive with conditional, e.g. 'Si tuviera tiempo, viajaria'.

skills.name: Pluperfect and conditional perfect
skills.description: Form 'habia comido', 'habria ido' and the perfect subjunctive to sequence past events.

skills.name: Subjunctive in adverbial and adjective clauses
skills.description: Choose mood after conjunctions like 'para que', 'cuando', 'aunque' and in clauses describing unknown antecedents, e.g. 'Busco un libro que sea interesante'.

topics.name: Spanish grammar: passive, register and nuance

skills.name: Passive voice and alternatives
skills.description: Convert 'La empresa construyo el puente' to 'El puente fue construido por la empresa' or to a se construction.

skills.name: Register and politeness
skills.description: Rewrite or pick phrases to shift from informal to formal register, e.g. 'Dame eso' to 'Podria darmelo, por favor?'

skills.name: Ser and estar with changing meaning
skills.description: Choose ser or estar where the adjective shifts meaning, e.g. 'es listo' (clever) versus 'esta listo' (ready).

skills.name: Reported speech
skills.description: Convert direct quotes to reported speech with tense shifts, e.g. 'Dijo: Vendre' becomes 'Dijo que vendria'.

skills.name: Literary analysis
skills.description: Read an excerpt from a novel or play and identify narrative point of view, symbolism and theme.

skills.name: Editorials and argument
skills.description: Read an editorial and identify the thesis, evidence and a counterargument, labelling each part.

skills.name: Historical and official documents
skills.description: Read a simplified historical speech or constitution excerpt and infer its purpose and audience.

skills.name: Podcasts and news reports
skills.description: Listen to a one-minute news or podcast clip and identify the main claim and two supporting details.

skills.name: Understanding regional accents
skills.description: Identify the likely region of a speaker from features such as vosotros, voseo or aspirated s, and understand the message.

skills.name: Debating and conceding points
skills.description: Pick phrases to agree, disagree and concede, e.g. 'Aunque es cierto que..., no estoy de acuerdo con...', in a structured exchange.

skills.name: Job and university interviews
skills.description: Choose appropriate formal responses to interview questions, e.g. 'Hableme de sus fortalezas'.

skills.name: Cultural comparison
skills.description: Build a comparison statement with 'mientras que' or 'a diferencia de' between two Spanish-speaking cultures and your own.

skills.name: Argumentative essay structure
skills.description: Order the parts of a persuasive essay and select the thesis statement that fits the given evidence.

skills.name: Integrating sources
skills.description: Choose the sentence that correctly cites a source, e.g. 'Segun el articulo, ...', without copying it word for word.

skills.name: Advanced editing
skills.description: Find and correct errors in mood, pronoun placement, accents and por/para in a paragraph.

topics.name: Spanish culture: the contemporary Spanish-speaking world

skills.name: Cinema
skills.description: Match directors and films such as Almodovar, del Toro and 'Roma' to countries and themes.

skills.name: Current affairs and institutions
skills.description: Identify institutions and issues such as the European Union, Mercosur and migration in the context of Spanish-speaking countries.

skills.name: Literary movements
skills.description: Place movements such as the Golden Age, modernismo and magical realism on a timeline and match representative authors.

skills.name: Spanish as a global language
skills.description: Answer facts about Spanish speaker numbers, Equatorial Guinea and the Philippines, and the role of the Real Academia Espanola.

skills.name: Keep a steady beat
skills.description: Tap along with a steady pulse and tell whether a pattern of taps is steady or uneven, e.g. choosing which of two clapping clips keeps the beat.

skills.name: High and low sounds
skills.description: Decide whether a sound or note is higher or lower than another, e.g. 'Is the second bell higher or lower?'

skills.name: Loud and quiet
skills.description: Classify sounds and musical moments as loud or quiet and match them to pictures, e.g. a lion roar is loud, a whisper is quiet.

skills.name: Fast and slow music
skills.description: Tell whether a piece of music is fast or slow and pick a matching movement, e.g. march for fast, sway for slow.

skills.name: Same or different
skills.description: Hear or see two short patterns and say if they are the same or different, e.g. ta ta ti-ti ta versus ta ta ta ta.

skills.name: Music and feelings
skills.description: Match a short piece of music to the feeling it suggests, e.g. happy, sleepy, scary or excited.

skills.name: Name classroom percussion
skills.description: Identify common classroom instruments from a picture or sound, e.g. drum, shaker, triangle, tambourine, xylophone.

skills.name: Shake, tap or scrape
skills.description: Sort instruments by how they are played, e.g. a maraca is shaken, a drum is tapped, a guiro is scraped.

skills.name: Echo a rhythm
skills.description: Repeat a short clapped rhythm by tapping it back in the same order, e.g. clap, clap, rest, clap.

skills.name: Call and response
skills.description: Pick the correct response phrase that answers a sung call, e.g. the leader sings 'Hello, friends' and the group answers 'Hello, teacher'.

skills.name: Speaking, whispering, singing, shouting
skills.description: Classify how a voice is being used, e.g. deciding whether a clip is singing or speaking.

skills.name: Kinds of lines
skills.description: Identify straight, curved, zigzag, wavy, thick and thin lines in a picture, e.g. 'Tap the zigzag line'.

skills.name: Basic shapes in art
skills.description: Find circles, squares, triangles and rectangles hidden in artworks and objects, e.g. the sun as a circle.

skills.name: Primary colours
skills.description: Name red, yellow and blue as the primary colours and pick them out of a set, e.g. 'Which colour is not a primary colour?'

skills.name: Name art tools
skills.description: Identify everyday art tools and materials, e.g. paintbrush, crayon, scissors, glue, clay.

skills.name: Choose the right tool
skills.description: Match a task to the tool that does it, e.g. use scissors to cut paper and a brush to spread paint.

skills.name: Studio safety and clean-up
skills.description: Put the steps of using and cleaning a material in order, e.g. wet brush, paint, rinse brush, dry brush.

skills.name: Ta and ti-ti
skills.description: Read and clap rhythm patterns written with ta (one sound per beat) and ti-ti (two sounds per beat), e.g. tap back 'ta ti-ti ta ta'.

skills.name: The silent beat
skills.description: Recognise a beat with no sound in a pattern and show it with a rest symbol or 'sh', e.g. 'ta ta sh ta'.

skills.name: So and mi
skills.description: Tell so (higher) from mi (lower) in a two-note tune and place notes high or low on a two-line staff, e.g. 'so-mi-so-so-mi'.

skills.name: Verse and chorus
skills.description: Tell which part of a song repeats with the same words (chorus) and which changes (verse), e.g. labelling sections of a familiar song.

skills.name: Speeding up and slowing down
skills.description: Decide whether music gets faster, slower or stays the same, e.g. a train leaving a station speeds up.

skills.name: Instrument or voice
skills.description: Classify what makes a sound in a clip as a voice, a drum, a string instrument or a wind instrument.

skills.name: Pitched or unpitched
skills.description: Sort instruments into those that can play a tune (xylophone, recorder) and those that keep rhythm only (drum, shaker).

skills.name: Big is low, small is high
skills.description: Predict which of two instruments or bars sounds lower, e.g. the longer xylophone bar sounds lower.

skills.name: Meet the orchestra
skills.description: Identify a violin, trumpet, flute and drum from a picture and know which is played by bowing, blowing or hitting.

skills.name: Why people make music
skills.description: Match a type of song to its purpose, e.g. lullaby for sleeping, march for parading, work song for working together.

skills.name: Songs from many places
skills.description: Connect a well-known children's song or instrument to the region it comes from, e.g. the djembe drum from West Africa.

skills.name: Secondary colours
skills.description: Predict the colour made by mixing two primaries, e.g. red + yellow = orange, and name orange, green and purple as secondary colours.

skills.name: Warm and cool colours
skills.description: Sort colours into warm (red, orange, yellow) and cool (blue, green, purple) and say which a picture mostly uses.

skills.name: Describing texture
skills.description: Match texture words to pictures of surfaces, e.g. rough bark, smooth glass, fluffy cotton, bumpy pebbles.

skills.name: Continue the pattern
skills.description: Work out what comes next in a repeating shape or colour pattern, e.g. circle, square, circle, square, ?

skills.name: Symmetry in art
skills.description: Decide whether a picture is symmetrical and pick the half that completes a mirror image, e.g. a butterfly's wings.

skills.name: Front and back
skills.description: Say which objects in a picture are in front (foreground) and which are far behind (background), e.g. the tree is in front of the mountains.

skills.name: Portrait, landscape or still life
skills.description: Classify an artwork by what it shows: a person (portrait), scenery (landscape) or arranged objects (still life).

skills.name: Art we use every day
skills.description: Spot where art appears in daily life and who makes it, e.g. a book illustration is drawn by an illustrator, a building is designed by an architect.

skills.name: Note values
skills.description: Identify quarter, half, whole and paired eighth notes by shape and say how many beats each lasts, e.g. a half note lasts 2 beats in 4/4.

skills.name: Rests
skills.description: Identify quarter, half and whole rests, match each rest to the note of the same length, and find the rest in a written rhythm.

skills.name: Measures and bar lines
skills.description: Count the beats inside a measure and spot where a bar line belongs, e.g. splitting 'quarter quarter half quarter quarter half' into two measures of 4 beats.

skills.name: ABA form
skills.description: Label the sections of a short piece as A or B and recognise ABA (same, different, same), e.g. labelling 'Twinkle, Twinkle' phrases.

skills.name: Tempo words
skills.description: Match basic Italian tempo words to speeds, e.g. allegro is fast, andante is walking pace, adagio is slow.

skills.name: Four instrument families
skills.description: Sort orchestra instruments into strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion, e.g. a clarinet is a woodwind.

skills.name: So, mi and la
skills.description: Read and order three-note solfege tunes on a staff, e.g. arranging so-la-so-mi to match the notes shown.

skills.name: Rounds and partner songs
skills.description: Understand that in a round the same tune starts at different times and pick when the second group should begin, e.g. 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat'.

skills.name: Good singing habits
skills.description: Choose the habits that help singing, e.g. standing tall and breathing from the belly rather than lifting the shoulders.

skills.name: Folk music by region
skills.description: Match a folk instrument or dance to its region, e.g. bagpipes with Scotland, mariachi with Mexico, taiko with Japan.

skills.name: Meet a composer
skills.description: Recognise a few famous composers and one well-known piece each, e.g. Beethoven and his Fifth Symphony, Tchaikovsky and The Nutcracker.

skills.name: Light and dark values
skills.description: Order shades from lightest to darkest and tell which part of a picture is lightest, e.g. ordering five grey swatches.

skills.name: Shape or form
skills.description: Tell flat shapes (circle, square) from 3D forms (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone) and match each shape to its form.

skills.name: Overlapping for space
skills.description: Decide which object is closer when shapes overlap and which is bigger because it is nearer, e.g. the overlapping apple is in front.

skills.name: Build the colour wheel
skills.description: Place the six primary and secondary colours in order around the wheel, e.g. red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

skills.name: Complementary pairs
skills.description: Match each colour with its opposite on the wheel, e.g. red with green, blue with orange, yellow with purple.

skills.name: Tints and shades
skills.description: Know that adding white makes a tint and adding black makes a shade, and pick the tint or shade of a given colour.

skills.name: Name the technique
skills.description: Look at an artwork and tell whether it is a painting, drawing, collage, print or sculpture, e.g. cut paper glued in layers is collage.

skills.name: Steps of a simple print
skills.description: Order the steps of making a stamp print: carve or build the block, roll on ink, press onto paper, lift.

skills.name: Clay basics
skills.description: Match clay techniques to their names, e.g. pinch pot, coil, slab, and know that scoring and slipping joins pieces.

skills.name: Art forms around the world
skills.description: Match traditional art forms to their cultures, e.g. origami with Japan, Adinkra cloth with Ghana, totem poles with Pacific Northwest First Nations.

skills.name: Masks, patterns and meaning
skills.description: Explain what a traditional object was used for, e.g. a mask for a ceremony or a woven pattern to tell a family story.

skills.name: Time signatures
skills.description: Read 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 time signatures, say how many beats are in each measure, and pick the signature that fits a written measure.

skills.name: Reading rhythm
skills.description: Fill a measure with notes and rests so the beats add up to the time signature, e.g. quarter + quarter + half in 4/4, and tap a written rhythm in order.

skills.name: Dotted notes and ties
skills.description: Work out the length of a dotted note or tied notes, e.g. a dotted half note lasts 3 beats and two tied quarter notes last 2 beats.

skills.name: Do, re, mi, so, la
skills.description: Read five-note solfege melodies on the staff and order the syllables from lowest to highest, e.g. do-re-mi-so-la.

skills.name: Melody goes up, down or stays
skills.description: Describe the direction of a melody or pick the contour drawing that matches a tune, e.g. a melody that steps up then leaps down.

skills.name: Steps, leaps and repeats
skills.description: Classify each move between two notes as a step (neighbouring notes), a leap (skipping notes) or a repeat.

skills.name: Orchestra instruments by family
skills.description: Name specific instruments (oboe, cello, tuba, timpani) and sort them into their family.

skills.name: How sound is made
skills.description: Match how an instrument vibrates to the instrument, e.g. a reed for clarinet, buzzing lips for trumpet, a bowed string for violin, a struck skin for drum.

skills.name: Choir, band and orchestra
skills.description: Tell ensembles apart by who plays in them, e.g. a choir sings, a concert band has no strings, an orchestra has strings.

skills.name: Rondo and other forms
skills.description: Label section patterns such as AB, ABA and ABACA (rondo) from a description or listening map.

skills.name: Melody and accompaniment
skills.description: Identify which part carries the tune and which parts support it, e.g. the singer has the melody while the guitar strums chords.

skills.name: Solo, duet, trio, group
skills.description: Count performers in a description or picture and name the grouping, e.g. two singers make a duet.

skills.name: Name the style
skills.description: Match descriptions or typical instruments to styles such as classical, jazz, folk, rock and pop, e.g. improvised saxophone solos suggest jazz.

skills.name: Instruments of each style
skills.description: Sort instruments into the style they are most linked with, e.g. electric guitar with rock, banjo with bluegrass, sitar with Indian classical.

skills.name: Positive and negative space
skills.description: Identify the object (positive space) and the empty area around it (negative space) in a silhouette or cut-out.

skills.name: Simple proportion
skills.description: Spot the figure or face with believable proportions, e.g. eyes halfway down the head and arms reaching to mid-thigh.

skills.name: Real and implied texture
skills.description: Tell real texture you can feel (thick paint, collage) from implied texture that is only drawn, e.g. pencil fur marks.

topics.name: Principles of design: balance, rhythm, emphasis

skills.name: Symmetrical, asymmetrical, radial
skills.description: Classify a composition's balance, e.g. a mandala is radial, a lopsided but steady layout is asymmetrical.

skills.name: Rhythm and repetition
skills.description: Find the repeated element that creates rhythm in a design and classify it as regular, alternating or progressive.

skills.name: Emphasis and focal point
skills.description: Point to the focal point of an artwork and say what makes it stand out, e.g. the only red shape among greys.

skills.name: Horizon line
skills.description: Find the horizon line in a landscape and know that objects near it look farther away.

skills.name: Size, overlap and placement
skills.description: Use size, overlap and placement to say which object is nearest, e.g. the biggest, lowest, overlapping tree is closest.

skills.name: Foreground, middle ground, background
skills.description: Sort the parts of a scene into foreground, middle ground and background, e.g. flowers, a house, distant hills.

skills.name: Notes on the treble staff
skills.description: Name the letter of a note on the treble clef staff (lines E G B D F, spaces F A C E) and place a named note on the staff, e.g. the note on the second line is G.

skills.name: Tempo and dynamic markings
skills.description: Read tempo words (largo, andante, allegro, presto) and dynamic symbols (pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff, crescendo, decrescendo) and order them from slowest to fastest or quietest to loudest.

skills.name: Sharps, flats and naturals
skills.description: Explain what a sharp, flat or natural does to a note and name the altered note, e.g. a sharp before F makes F-sharp, a half step higher.

skills.name: Compose a four-bar rhythm
skills.description: Build four complete measures in 4/4 or 3/4 from a palette of note and rest tiles, e.g. 3/4: dotted half | quarter quarter quarter | half quarter | dotted half.

skills.name: Ostinato patterns
skills.description: Recognise an ostinato as a short repeating pattern and pick the pattern that would loop cleanly under a melody.

skills.name: Question and answer phrases
skills.description: Choose an answer phrase that ends on do to finish a question phrase that ends on so, making a complete musical sentence.

skills.name: Instruments of the world
skills.description: Match world instruments to their region and family, e.g. sitar (India, string), djembe (West Africa, percussion), didgeridoo (Australia, wind), erhu (China, string).

skills.name: Voice types
skills.description: Order soprano, alto, tenor and bass from highest to lowest and classify a described singer, e.g. the lowest male voice is bass.

skills.name: Major or minor
skills.description: Decide whether a melody or chord sounds major (brighter) or minor (darker) and match each to a typical mood or scene.

skills.name: Unison and harmony
skills.description: Tell whether voices sing the same notes together (unison) or different notes that fit together (harmony).

skills.name: Repetition and contrast
skills.description: Identify when a section repeats a previous idea and when it brings something new, and label a form such as AABA.

skills.name: Order the periods
skills.description: Place Baroque, Classical, Romantic and Modern periods in chronological order with a rough century for each.

skills.name: Composer to period
skills.description: Match composers to their period, e.g. Bach and Vivaldi (Baroque), Mozart and Haydn (Classical), Chopin and Brahms (Romantic).

skills.name: Famous pieces
skills.description: Match well-known pieces to their composers, e.g. The Four Seasons to Vivaldi, Fur Elise to Beethoven, Peter and the Wolf to Prokofiev.

skills.name: Analogous colours
skills.description: Pick sets of neighbouring colours on the wheel, e.g. blue, blue-green and green form an analogous scheme.

skills.name: Monochromatic schemes
skills.description: Recognise a design built from tints and shades of one hue and spot the swatch that breaks the scheme.

skills.name: Colour and mood
skills.description: Match a colour scheme to the feeling it commonly suggests, e.g. cool blues feel calm, hot reds and oranges feel energetic.

skills.name: Intermediate colours
skills.description: Name the colour between a primary and a secondary, e.g. blue + green = blue-green (teal), and place it on a 12-step wheel.

topics.name: Principles of design: unity, variety, movement

skills.name: Unity and variety
skills.description: Judge which composition feels unified yet varied, and name what ties it together, e.g. repeated colour with different shapes.

skills.name: Movement and direction
skills.description: Trace the path the eye follows in a composition and identify the lines or shapes that create movement, e.g. diagonal brush strokes.

skills.name: Contrast
skills.description: Identify the type of contrast used (light-dark, big-small, rough-smooth, warm-cool) in a design.

skills.name: Vanishing point
skills.description: Find the vanishing point where receding lines meet, e.g. railway tracks, and pick the drawing with correct one-point perspective.

skills.name: Draw a box in one-point perspective
skills.description: Order the steps: draw horizon line, mark vanishing point, draw front face, connect corners to the point, add the back edges.

skills.name: Light source and shadow
skills.description: Given a light source, pick which side of a form is lit and where the cast shadow falls, e.g. light from the left means shadow on the right.

skills.name: Notes on the bass clef
skills.description: Name notes on the bass clef staff (lines G B D F A, spaces A C E G) and relate middle C between the two staves.

skills.name: Build a major scale
skills.description: Apply the whole-whole-half-whole-whole-whole-half pattern to build a major scale from a given note, e.g. G major needs F-sharp.

skills.name: Interval size
skills.description: Count the interval number between two notes (2nd through octave), e.g. C up to G is a 5th.

skills.name: 6/8 and syncopation
skills.description: Read 6/8 as two groups of three eighths, fill 6/8 measures correctly, and spot syncopated patterns that stress off-beats.

skills.name: Phrases and cadence points
skills.description: Divide a melody into phrases and pick where a phrase breathes or ends, e.g. a four-bar phrase ending on a long note.

skills.name: I, IV and V
skills.description: Name the root notes of chords I, IV and V in a given major key, e.g. in C major they are C, F and G.

skills.name: Compose in 6/8
skills.description: Build a two-measure rhythm in 6/8 from note tiles so each measure totals six eighth notes.

skills.name: Monophonic, homophonic, polyphonic
skills.description: Classify a described or heard excerpt by texture, e.g. one unaccompanied melody is monophonic; melody with chords is homophonic; independent melodies at once is polyphonic.

skills.name: Theme and variations
skills.description: Identify how a variation changes the theme (rhythm, mode, tempo, ornament) and order variations as described.

skills.name: Describing timbre
skills.description: Match timbre words (bright, dark, nasal, mellow, brassy) to the instruments or sounds they fit, e.g. a muted trumpet is nasal.

skills.name: Gamelan and West African drumming
skills.description: Identify key features of Indonesian gamelan (layered metallophones, cyclic gongs) and West African drumming (polyrhythm, call and response, master drummer).

skills.name: Latin American rhythms
skills.description: Match rhythms and styles to their origins, e.g. samba with Brazil, tango with Argentina, salsa with Cuba and Puerto Rico, and recognise the clave pattern.

skills.name: Roots of the blues
skills.description: Describe the blues as African American music with 12-bar form, blue notes and AAB lyric pattern, and identify the AAB pattern in a verse.

skills.name: Line quality and expression
skills.description: Match line qualities (gestural, contour, hatching, cross-hatching, implied) to examples and to the feeling they create.

skills.name: Nine-step value scale
skills.description: Order values from white to black and pick the swatch that fits a gap in a value scale.

skills.name: Geometric and organic shapes
skills.description: Sort shapes into geometric (precise, mathematical) and organic (free-form, natural) and say which an artwork mostly uses.

skills.name: Proportion and scale
skills.description: Tell proportion (parts relative to each other) from scale (size relative to the viewer or surroundings), and spot deliberate exaggeration, e.g. an oversized sculpture of a spoon.

skills.name: Visual hierarchy
skills.description: Order the elements of a poster by the sequence a viewer notices them, based on size, contrast and placement.

skills.name: Name the principle
skills.description: Given a description of what an artist did, name the design principle at work, e.g. repeating a shape across the canvas is rhythm.

skills.name: Two-point perspective
skills.description: Recognise two vanishing points on the horizon when a box is seen from a corner and pick the correctly constructed drawing.

skills.name: Atmospheric perspective
skills.description: Know that distant objects look paler, bluer and less detailed, and order mountains from nearest to farthest by their colour and detail.

skills.name: Eye level and viewpoint
skills.description: Decide whether a scene is viewed from above (bird's-eye), below (worm's-eye) or at eye level from where the horizon sits.

skills.name: Egypt, Greece and Rome
skills.description: Match artworks and features to their civilisation, e.g. hieroglyphs and profile figures to Egypt, idealised marble statues to Greece, the Colosseum and arches to Rome.

skills.name: Medieval art
skills.description: Identify features of Byzantine mosaics, illuminated manuscripts and Gothic cathedrals, e.g. gold backgrounds and stained glass.

skills.name: Asian and African traditions
skills.description: Connect artworks to their traditions, e.g. Chinese ink landscape scrolls, Japanese ukiyo-e prints, Benin bronzes, Great Zimbabwe stonework.

skills.name: Key signatures
skills.description: Name the major key from a key signature of up to three sharps or flats using the order F C G D A E B, e.g. two sharps is D major.

skills.name: Natural minor scales
skills.description: Find the relative minor of a major key (three half steps below) and build a natural minor scale, e.g. A minor shares C major's notes.

skills.name: Interval quality
skills.description: Label intervals as major, minor or perfect, e.g. C to E is a major third and C to E-flat is a minor third.

skills.name: Build triads
skills.description: Stack root, third and fifth to build major and minor triads, e.g. D major is D, F-sharp, A.

skills.name: Common chord progressions
skills.description: Recognise and complete progressions like I-V-vi-IV or I-IV-V-I in a given key, e.g. in G major: G, D, Em, C.

skills.name: Melody that fits the chords
skills.description: Choose melody notes that belong to the chord sounding underneath, e.g. over a C chord prefer C, E or G on strong beats.

skills.name: Verse, chorus and bridge
skills.description: Order the sections of a typical pop song (intro, verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus) and describe the job of each.

topics.name: Harmony and cadence by ear and eye

skills.name: Major, minor, diminished
skills.description: Identify the quality of a written or heard chord from its thirds, e.g. a minor third plus a minor third is diminished.

skills.name: Finished or unfinished
skills.description: Tell a V-I ending (authentic cadence, sounds finished) from a phrase stopping on V (half cadence, sounds unfinished).

skills.name: Instrumentation in recordings
skills.description: List which instruments play in a described arrangement and classify the ensemble, e.g. drums, bass, two guitars and a singer is a rock band.

skills.name: Traits of each period
skills.description: Match stylistic traits to periods, e.g. harpsichord and ornamentation to Baroque, balanced phrases to Classical, large orchestras and emotion to Romantic.

skills.name: Forms and genres of each period
skills.description: Connect genres to the period that developed them, e.g. fugue and concerto grosso to Baroque, symphony and string quartet to Classical, art song and programme music to Romantic.

skills.name: Composer timeline
skills.description: Order composers by lifetime, e.g. Monteverdi, Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Schumann, Tchaikovsky.

skills.name: Jazz styles
skills.description: Order and describe jazz styles (ragtime, Dixieland, swing, bebop, cool, fusion) and match key figures, e.g. Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Charlie Parker, Miles Davis.

skills.name: Rock and pop decades
skills.description: Place rock and pop developments by decade, e.g. rock and roll in the 1950s, the British Invasion in the 1960s, punk in the 1970s.

skills.name: Elements of hip-hop
skills.description: Identify the core elements of hip-hop culture (MCing, DJing, breaking, graffiti) and techniques like sampling and beat-making.

skills.name: Hue, saturation and value
skills.description: Describe a colour by its three properties and pick which property changed between two swatches, e.g. the hue stayed red but saturation dropped.

skills.name: Triadic and split-complementary
skills.description: Identify triadic schemes (three evenly spaced hues) and split-complementary schemes (a hue plus the two neighbours of its complement).

skills.name: Colour temperature and depth
skills.description: Know that warm, saturated colours advance and cool, dull colours recede, and pick the colour choice that pushes a shape back.

skills.name: Painting techniques
skills.description: Match techniques to descriptions, e.g. wet-on-wet watercolour blooms, dry brush, glazing with thin layers, impasto thick paint.

skills.name: Drawing media
skills.description: Identify graphite grades (H hard, B soft), charcoal, ink and pastel from descriptions of their marks and best uses.

skills.name: Relief, intaglio, screen
skills.description: Classify printmaking methods by whether the raised surface (relief), the cut groove (intaglio) or a stencil (screen) carries the ink.

skills.name: Ceramics process
skills.description: Order the stages of pottery: wet clay, leather-hard, bone-dry, bisque fire, glaze, glaze fire.

topics.name: Renaissance and Baroque, Islamic and East Asian art

skills.name: Renaissance masters
skills.description: Match artists to works and innovations, e.g. Leonardo and the Mona Lisa, Michelangelo and the Sistine ceiling, Brunelleschi and linear perspective.

skills.name: Baroque drama
skills.description: Identify Baroque traits such as chiaroscuro, diagonal movement and emotional intensity, e.g. in Caravaggio and Rembrandt.

skills.name: Islamic and East Asian art
skills.description: Recognise geometric pattern, arabesque and calligraphy in Islamic art and brush landscape, calligraphy and woodblock print in Chinese, Japanese and Korean art.

topics.name: Seventh chords, inversions and advanced rhythm

skills.name: Seventh chords
skills.description: Build and identify dominant seventh, major seventh and minor seventh chords, e.g. G7 is G, B, D, F.

skills.name: Chord inversions
skills.description: Identify whether a triad is in root position, first inversion or second inversion from its lowest note, e.g. E-G-C is C major in first inversion.

skills.name: Transposition
skills.description: Move a short melody up or down by a given interval, e.g. transpose C-D-E up a perfect fourth to F-G-A.

skills.name: Triplets and odd meters
skills.description: Read triplets (three in the time of two) and count measures in 5/4 and 7/8, e.g. grouping 7/8 as 2+2+3.

skills.name: Transform a motif
skills.description: Identify how a motif was transformed: sequence (repeated higher or lower), inversion (mirrored), retrograde (backwards), augmentation (longer notes), diminution (shorter notes).

skills.name: Arranging roles
skills.description: Assign melody, harmony, bass and rhythm roles to instruments of a small ensemble so every role is covered, e.g. bass guitar takes the bass line.

skills.name: Setting words to rhythm
skills.description: Place stressed syllables on strong beats, e.g. 'to-MOR-row' should put MOR on the downbeat.

skills.name: Binary and ternary form
skills.description: Label a piece AB (binary) or ABA (ternary) from a section map and identify rounded binary.

skills.name: Sonata and rondo outlines
skills.description: Order the sections of sonata form (exposition, development, recapitulation) and recognise the returning A of rondo.

skills.name: Major, minor or modal
skills.description: Tell major from minor and spot a modal flavour such as Dorian's raised sixth or Mixolydian's lowered seventh in a described scale.

skills.name: Twentieth-century styles
skills.description: Match styles to traits and composers, e.g. Impressionism with Debussy, atonality with Schoenberg, minimalism with Glass, and order them by decade.

skills.name: History of recorded sound
skills.description: Order recording technologies: phonograph cylinder, 78 rpm disc, vinyl LP, cassette, CD, MP3, streaming.

skills.name: Electronic music pioneers
skills.description: Connect inventions and pioneers to their contribution, e.g. the theremin, Moog synthesiser, drum machine and the first use of multitrack recording.

topics.name: Global popular music and film music

skills.name: Global popular styles
skills.description: Match global popular genres to their origin and traits, e.g. reggae (Jamaica, off-beat skank), K-pop (South Korea, idol groups), Afrobeats (West Africa), Bollywood film song (India).

skills.name: What film music does
skills.description: Identify the function of a cue: setting place and time, signalling a character (leitmotif), building tension or guiding emotion.

skills.name: Genre fusions
skills.description: Name the parent genres of a fusion style, e.g. ska-punk blends ska and punk; jazz fusion blends jazz and rock.

skills.name: Rule of thirds
skills.description: Place the subject on a thirds intersection and judge which crop follows the rule of thirds.

skills.name: Golden ratio and spiral
skills.description: Recognise the golden ratio (about 1.618) in rectangles and spirals and compute the longer side given the shorter, e.g. 10 cm gives about 16.2 cm.

skills.name: Gestalt grouping
skills.description: Name the gestalt principle at work: proximity, similarity, closure, continuity or figure-ground, e.g. a broken circle still read as a circle is closure.

skills.name: Cropping and framing
skills.description: Choose the crop that strengthens a focal point or implies movement, and spot distracting edge elements.

skills.name: Impressionism and Post-Impressionism
skills.description: Match traits and artists, e.g. visible brushwork and light effects with Monet, pointillism with Seurat, expressive colour with Van Gogh.

skills.name: Cubism, Surrealism and Abstraction
skills.description: Identify movements from traits, e.g. fragmented multiple viewpoints (Cubism, Picasso), dreamlike scenes (Surrealism, Dali), non-representational drips (Abstract Expressionism, Pollock).

skills.name: Pop Art
skills.description: Recognise Pop Art's use of consumer imagery, repetition and comic style, e.g. Warhol's soup cans and Lichtenstein's Ben-Day dots.

skills.name: Order the movements
skills.description: Place art movements in order: Realism, Impressionism, Post-Impressionism, Cubism, Surrealism, Abstract Expressionism, Pop Art.

skills.name: Raster or vector
skills.description: Tell raster images (pixels, lose quality when enlarged) from vector images (paths, scale cleanly) and pick the right type for a job, e.g. a logo should be vector.

skills.name: Layers and resolution
skills.description: Explain what layers do and compute pixel dimensions from size and resolution, e.g. 4 inches at 300 ppi is 1200 pixels.

skills.name: Typography basics
skills.description: Identify serif, sans-serif, script and display typefaces and name parts of type such as baseline, x-height and kerning.

skills.name: Photo composition
skills.description: Identify leading lines, framing, symmetry and depth of field in a photograph description and choose the technique that fits a goal.

skills.name: Roman numeral analysis
skills.description: Label each diatonic triad in a major or minor key with Roman numerals showing quality, e.g. in C major the chord D-F-A is ii.

skills.name: Cadence types
skills.description: Classify cadences as perfect authentic, imperfect authentic, half, plagal or deceptive from the chords and soprano, e.g. V to vi is deceptive.

skills.name: Inversion symbols
skills.description: Read and write inversion figures (6, 6/4, 7, 6/5, 4/3, 4/2) for triads and seventh chords, e.g. V6/5 is a dominant seventh in first inversion.

skills.name: Non-chord tones
skills.description: Identify passing tones, neighbour tones, suspensions and anticipations in a melody over given chords.

skills.name: Four-part voice leading
skills.description: Spot errors in SATB writing such as parallel fifths, parallel octaves, voice crossing and unresolved leading tones.

skills.name: Harmonise a melody
skills.description: Choose a chord for each melody note that contains it and follows common progressions, e.g. a melody G in C major on a strong beat could take I or V.

skills.name: Period and sentence structure
skills.description: Identify antecedent and consequent phrases, parallel versus contrasting periods, and the sentence's presentation-continuation shape.

skills.name: Chant to polyphony
skills.description: Order developments from Gregorian chant through organum to Renaissance polyphony and match figures like Hildegard, Machaut, Josquin and Palestrina.

skills.name: Renaissance music
skills.description: Identify Renaissance traits (imitative polyphony, modal harmony, a cappella mass and motet, madrigal word-painting) and the rise of printed music.

skills.name: Baroque genres and figures
skills.description: Match fugue, concerto grosso, opera, oratorio and suite to their traits and to Bach, Handel, Vivaldi, Monteverdi and Purcell.

skills.name: Twelve-bar blues
skills.description: Build the standard 12-bar blues progression in a given key (I I I I, IV IV I I, V IV I I) and identify the blues scale notes.

skills.name: Jazz vocabulary
skills.description: Define and apply terms such as swing feel, comping, walking bass, head, chorus, trading fours and improvisation over changes.

skills.name: Scales of the world
skills.description: Match scale systems to traditions, e.g. raga to Indian classical, maqam to Arabic music, pentatonic to Chinese and many folk traditions, and identify a pentatonic set.

skills.name: Describe, analyse, interpret, judge
skills.description: Order the four steps of art criticism and classify a statement by step, e.g. 'the red draws the eye to the figure' is analysis.

skills.name: Elements in a specific work
skills.description: Identify which element of art (line, shape, form, value, colour, texture, space) a description of an artwork is about.

skills.name: Medium, technique and support
skills.description: Separate a work's medium (oil), technique (glazing) and support (canvas) from a caption, e.g. 'tempera on wood panel'.

skills.name: Principles in masterworks
skills.description: Name the dominant design principle in a described famous work, e.g. the diagonal movement in Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People.

skills.name: Grid systems
skills.description: Identify columns, gutters and margins in a layout grid and choose the grid that fits a brief, e.g. a three-column grid for a newsletter.

skills.name: Typographic hierarchy
skills.description: Order text elements (headline, subhead, body, caption) by size and weight for a clear hierarchy and spot a layout where it breaks.

topics.name: Prehistoric to classical and early global art

skills.name: Prehistoric and Mesopotamian art
skills.description: Match works to cultures and purposes, e.g. Lascaux cave paintings, the Venus of Willendorf, Stonehenge, the Standard of Ur and the Code of Hammurabi stele.

skills.name: Egyptian conventions
skills.description: Identify Egyptian conventions such as composite view, hierarchic scale, the canon of proportions and funerary purpose, e.g. in the Palette of Narmer.

skills.name: Greek periods and Roman adaptation
skills.description: Order Geometric, Archaic, Classical and Hellenistic periods, match statues to them (kouros, Doryphoros, Laocoon) and name Roman innovations like concrete and veristic portraits.

skills.name: Early global traditions
skills.description: Connect works to cultures, e.g. Olmec colossal heads, Nok terracottas, the Gupta Buddha, the Terracotta Army of Qin.

skills.name: Drawing techniques
skills.description: Match contour, gesture, blind contour, hatching, cross-hatching, stippling and blending to descriptions and purposes.

skills.name: Painting methods and media
skills.description: Compare oil, acrylic, watercolour, gouache, tempera and fresco by drying time, opacity and surface, e.g. fresco is painted into wet plaster.

skills.name: Lithography, etching and screen print
skills.description: Order the steps of an etching or screen print and classify lithography as planographic.

skills.name: Secondary dominants
skills.description: Identify and spell secondary dominants such as V/V and V/ii, e.g. in C major D-F-sharp-A-C is V7/V.

skills.name: Modulation to closely related keys
skills.description: Name the closely related keys of a given key and identify a pivot chord that belongs to both keys.

skills.name: The seven modes
skills.description: Build and identify Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian and Locrian from their characteristic notes, e.g. Lydian has a raised fourth.

skills.name: Borrowed chords
skills.description: Recognise chords borrowed from the parallel minor (iv, bVI, bVII) in a major-key progression, e.g. F minor in C major.

skills.name: First and second species
skills.description: Apply species rules: consonant intervals only in first species, begin and end on perfect consonances, avoid parallel perfects, and spot a rule break in a two-voice example.

skills.name: Ranges and transposing instruments
skills.description: Match orchestral instruments to their ranges and transpositions, e.g. a written C for B-flat clarinet sounds B-flat.

skills.name: Lead-sheet chord symbols
skills.description: Translate chord symbols to notes and back, e.g. Dm7 is D-F-A-C, and read slash chords and sus chords.

skills.name: Sonata form in detail
skills.description: Identify the key areas and sections of sonata form (exposition with modulating transition, development, recapitulation, coda) in a described movement.

skills.name: Growth of the symphony
skills.description: Trace how the symphony changed from Haydn to Beethoven to Mahler in length, orchestra size and expression.

skills.name: Nationalism and programme music
skills.description: Match Romantic composers to national styles and programmatic works, e.g. Smetana and Ma Vlast, Grieg and Norway, Berlioz and the Symphonie fantastique.

topics.name: Jazz harmony, production and musical theatre

skills.name: ii-V-I and extensions
skills.description: Spell ii-V-I in a given key with sevenths and identify ninths and thirteenths in jazz voicings, e.g. in F major: Gm7, C7, Fmaj7.

skills.name: Elements of a pop production
skills.description: Identify production elements and their role, e.g. the hook, the drop, a four-on-the-floor kick, reverb for space, a side-chain pump.

skills.name: Opera and musical theatre
skills.description: Match terms and shows to forms, e.g. aria and recitative to opera, the book musical to Oklahoma!, the concept musical to Sondheim.

skills.name: Frequency, amplitude and timbre
skills.description: Relate frequency to pitch and amplitude to loudness, and compute octaves, e.g. 440 Hz up an octave is 880 Hz.

skills.name: MIDI and the DAW
skills.description: Distinguish MIDI data from audio, read MIDI note numbers (60 is middle C) and name DAW parts such as track, clip, quantise and tempo map.

skills.name: Signal flow
skills.description: Order a recording chain: microphone, preamp, analogue-to-digital converter, DAW, digital-to-analogue converter, monitors.

skills.name: Three-point perspective
skills.description: Recognise a third vanishing point above or below for tall objects and pick the drawing that uses it correctly.

skills.name: Ellipses and cylinders
skills.description: Know that circles in perspective become ellipses that widen farther from eye level, and choose the correct ellipse for a cup's rim versus base.

skills.name: Figure proportions
skills.description: Apply the 7.5 to 8 head-height canon, e.g. the hips sit about four heads down, and spot proportion errors in a figure.

skills.name: Anatomy landmarks
skills.description: Match skeletal landmarks and major muscle groups to their location on a figure, e.g. clavicle, sternum, deltoid, patella.

skills.name: Fauvism and Expressionism
skills.description: Match works and artists, e.g. Matisse's arbitrary colour, Kirchner's angular city scenes, Munch's The Scream, Kandinsky's path to abstraction.

skills.name: Dada, De Stijl and Bauhaus
skills.description: Identify Dada's anti-art readymades (Duchamp), De Stijl's grids (Mondrian) and Bauhaus's union of art, craft and industry.

skills.name: Harlem Renaissance and Mexican Muralism
skills.description: Connect artists and themes, e.g. Aaron Douglas and Jacob Lawrence to Black American life, Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros to public murals of history and labour.

topics.name: Vector, colour modes and interface design

skills.name: Paths and Bezier curves
skills.description: Identify anchor points, handles and path segments and predict how moving a handle changes a curve.

skills.name: RGB, CMYK and HSB
skills.description: Choose RGB for screens and CMYK for print, read hex codes, and identify a colour from its values, e.g. #FF0000 is pure red.

skills.name: File formats
skills.description: Match formats to uses: JPEG for photos, PNG for transparency, SVG for vector, GIF for simple animation, PDF for print-ready documents.

skills.name: Interface design basics
skills.description: Identify UI components (button, input, nav bar, modal) and judge affordance and contrast, e.g. body text should meet a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

skills.name: Augmented sixth chords
skills.description: Spell and identify Italian, French and German augmented sixth chords and their resolution to V, e.g. in C: A-flat, C, F-sharp (Italian).

skills.name: Neapolitan sixth
skills.description: Recognise the Neapolitan (a major triad on the lowered second degree, usually in first inversion) and its typical move to V.

skills.name: Modal mixture and chromatic mediants
skills.description: Identify borrowed chords and chromatic third relations in a progression, e.g. C major to E major is a chromatic mediant.

skills.name: Jazz chord extensions and alterations
skills.description: Spell chords with 9ths, 11ths, 13ths and alterations, e.g. G7(b9,#11) is G, B, D, F, A-flat, C-sharp.

skills.name: Fugue techniques
skills.description: Identify subject, answer, countersubject, episode, stretto and real versus tonal answer in a fugue exposition description.

skills.name: Orchestrating for balance
skills.description: Choose doublings and dynamics that balance an orchestral texture, e.g. one flute cannot balance four horns at forte.

skills.name: From lead sheet to arrangement
skills.description: Order the steps of arranging a lead sheet: analyse harmony, set the groove, assign bass and comping, voice the melody, add counter-lines and intro/outro.

skills.name: Full formal analysis
skills.description: Map a movement's form (sonata, rondo, sonata-rondo, theme and variations) from thematic and key descriptions and label each section.

skills.name: Harmonic analysis of a passage
skills.description: Label a four- to eight-chord passage with Roman numerals and inversions, including applied chords, e.g. I - V6/5/IV - IV - V7 - I.

skills.name: Motivic analysis
skills.description: Trace a motif across a piece and classify each appearance as exact, transposed, inverted, retrograde, augmented or fragmented.

skills.name: Impressionism and early modernism
skills.description: Match traits and works, e.g. Debussy's whole-tone and parallel chords, Stravinsky's Rite of Spring rhythms, Bartok's folk-based modernism.

skills.name: Serialism and the Second Viennese School
skills.description: Identify Schoenberg, Berg and Webern, define a twelve-tone row and name total serialism's later extension to rhythm and dynamics.

skills.name: Post-war currents
skills.description: Match neoclassicism, musique concrete, chance music, minimalism and spectralism to composers like Stravinsky, Schaeffer, Cage, Reich and Grisey.

skills.name: Subtractive synthesis
skills.description: Order the signal path oscillator, filter, amplifier and identify ADSR envelope stages, e.g. a slow attack makes a pad swell in.

skills.name: EQ, compression and effects
skills.description: Choose the right tool for a mix problem, e.g. a high-pass filter to remove rumble, a compressor to even out vocal levels, reverb to add space.

skills.name: Microphone types and placement
skills.description: Match dynamic, condenser and ribbon microphones and polar patterns (cardioid, omni, figure-8) to recording situations.

skills.name: Minimalism and Conceptual art
skills.description: Identify Minimalism's industrial repetition (Judd, LeWitt) and Conceptual art's idea-over-object (Kosuth, Weiner) from descriptions.

skills.name: Installation, performance and video
skills.description: Match artists to practices, e.g. Yayoi Kusama's infinity rooms, Marina Abramovic's durational performance, Nam June Paik's video art.

skills.name: Street art and global contemporary
skills.description: Recognise street art's roots and figures (Basquiat, Banksy) and global contemporary artists such as El Anatsui, Ai Weiwei and Shirin Neshat.

skills.name: Postmodern ideas
skills.description: Define appropriation, pastiche, deconstruction and the end of the single grand narrative, and apply them to a described work, e.g. Sherrie Levine rephotographing Walker Evans.

skills.name: Imitationalism, formalism, emotionalism
skills.description: Classify a judgment about an artwork by its theory, e.g. 'it looks exactly like her' is imitationalism, 'the balance of shapes is perfect' is formalism.

skills.name: Critical lenses
skills.description: Identify the lens a reading uses (formalist, Marxist, feminist, postcolonial, psychoanalytic) from the questions it asks about a work.

skills.name: Symbolism and iconography
skills.description: Decode common symbols in Western and global art, e.g. a skull for mortality, a dog for fidelity, a lotus for purity.

skills.name: Appropriation, copyright and fair use
skills.description: Judge scenarios for likely fair use versus infringement and distinguish cultural appropriation from respectful cultural exchange.

skills.name: 3D modelling basics
skills.description: Identify vertices, edges, faces, meshes, UV maps and the three-point lighting setup (key, fill, back).

skills.name: Principles of animation
skills.description: Name the animation principle in a described motion, e.g. a ball flattening on impact is squash and stretch; a character leaning before a jump is anticipation.

skills.name: Exposure triangle
skills.description: Relate aperture, shutter speed and ISO to brightness, depth of field, motion blur and noise, e.g. f/2 gives a shallow depth of field.

skills.name: Pitch-class sets
skills.description: Convert notes to pitch-class integers (C = 0), find a set's normal form and interval content, e.g. {C, E, G} is {0, 4, 7}.

skills.name: Twelve-tone row operations
skills.description: Apply transposition, inversion, retrograde and retrograde-inversion to a row and identify which form a given row is.

skills.name: Polyrhythm and metric modulation
skills.description: Resolve 3:2 and 4:3 polyrhythms onto a common grid and compute the new tempo in a metric modulation, e.g. quarter = 120 becomes dotted quarter = 80.

skills.name: Extended techniques and notation
skills.description: Match symbols and terms to techniques such as col legno, sul ponticello, multiphonics, prepared piano and graphic notation.

skills.name: Compose in a style
skills.description: Select the harmonic, rhythmic and textural traits that make a passage read as a given style, e.g. Baroque chorale versus bebop head versus minimalist loop.

skills.name: Scoring to picture
skills.description: Apply leitmotif, underscoring, hit points and tempo-to-frame-rate maths, e.g. at 24 fps a 2-second cue is 48 frames, and choose where a cue should hit.

skills.name: Advanced orchestration
skills.description: Choose idiomatic writing for instruments (string harmonics, brass mutes, woodwind registers) and avoid impractical passages, e.g. a trill across the clarinet break.

skills.name: Identify period and composer from features
skills.description: Infer the period and a likely composer from a described excerpt's harmony, texture, instrumentation and form, e.g. terraced dynamics and basso continuo suggest Baroque.

skills.name: Comparative analysis
skills.description: Compare two settings of the same text or theme and identify differences in key, form, texture and expressive aim.

skills.name: Score error detection
skills.description: Find the measure where a notated score departs from a described performance in pitch or rhythm.

skills.name: Music as protest
skills.description: Match protest songs and movements across eras and regions, e.g. 'We Shall Overcome' and civil rights, Victor Jara and Chile, Fela Kuti and Nigeria.

skills.name: Nationalism, propaganda and censorship
skills.description: Analyse how states have used or suppressed music, e.g. Shostakovich under Soviet policy, 'degenerate music' labelling in Nazi Germany, Afrobeat under military rule.

skills.name: Globalisation of music
skills.description: Trace how recording, migration and streaming spread styles, e.g. the path from Jamaican sound systems to UK grime, and order key developments.

skills.name: Copyright and licensing
skills.description: Distinguish composition and sound-recording copyrights and match licence types to uses, e.g. a sync licence for a song in a film, a mechanical licence for a cover.

skills.name: Roles and revenue streams
skills.description: Match industry roles (producer, A&R, publisher, manager, curator, gallerist) to their jobs and identify revenue streams such as royalties, touring, commissions and sales.

skills.name: From studio to release
skills.description: Order the steps of releasing a recording: writing, pre-production, tracking, editing, mixing, mastering, distribution, promotion.

skills.name: Portfolios, statements and pricing
skills.description: Identify the parts of an artist statement and portfolio and compute a fair price from materials, hours and rate, e.g. 10 hours at 25 plus 40 materials is 290.

skills.name: Architecture through the ages
skills.description: Order and identify styles by features, e.g. Gothic pointed arches, Renaissance symmetry, Baroque drama, Modernist glass box, Brutalist concrete, Deconstructivist forms.

skills.name: Architects and landmark buildings
skills.description: Match architects to buildings, e.g. Gaudi and the Sagrada Familia, Le Corbusier and Villa Savoye, Zaha Hadid and the Heydar Aliyev Center.

skills.name: Themes in contemporary art
skills.description: Identify the theme a described contemporary work addresses, e.g. identity, migration, climate, surveillance, memory, and name a representative artist.

skills.name: Curatorial concepts
skills.description: Group artworks into a coherent exhibition concept and spot the work that does not fit the stated theme.

skills.name: Exhibition design
skills.description: Apply hanging conventions and visitor flow, e.g. centre lines at about 145-150 cm, label placement, and sightline sequencing.

skills.name: Structure of a critical review
skills.description: Order the parts of an art review (hook, description, context, analysis, evaluation) and classify sentences by part.

skills.name: UX design process
skills.description: Order the UX process (research, personas, user flows, wireframes, prototype, usability test, iterate) and classify an activity by stage.

skills.name: Motion graphics
skills.description: Identify keyframes, easing curves, frame rates and timing, e.g. ease-out makes an object decelerate into place; 30 fps for 3 seconds is 90 frames.

skills.name: Generative and AI art ethics
skills.description: Distinguish algorithmic, generative and AI-assisted art, and evaluate scenarios about training data consent, attribution and disclosure.

skills.name: Accessible design
skills.description: Apply accessibility rules such as alt text, colour-independent cues, minimum contrast and readable type size, and spot the inaccessible choice in a design.
